title: Agents: Stop replying after handoff on public/API and let teammates answer there
description:
On the Chat channel the agent goes silent after handoff (lib/agents-chat.ts checks wasHandedOff), but sendAgentMessage in lib/agents.ts never checks agent_conversations.handed_off, so on /a/<handle> and the API the bot keeps answering after it promised a teammate. Worse, components/agents/AgentConversations.tsx is read-only: the notification links to a transcript where nobody can reply, so the handoff is a dead end. Fin keeps the conversation owned and routes it to the right team with a reply path (https://fin.ai/capabilities). First scope: after handoff, store visitor messages without running the model, add a teammate reply box in the Conversations tab that streams into the public page via polling, and ask for an email at handoff time so the team can follow up offline.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Intercom Fin, Zapier Agents, Lindy (plus OpenAI AgentKit as reference for evals/versioning).

title: Agents: Fetch knowledge URLs on save and re-sync them daily from the cron tick
description:
Saving a new URL only inserts a 'pending' row (syncKnowledgeUrls in lib/agents.ts) and searchAgentKnowledge only reads status='ok', so a newly added page is invisible to the agent until someone clicks refresh in the Knowledge tab. There is no scheduled re-crawl (vercel.json only runs /api/cron/tick and robots, neither touches agents), so prices or policies on those pages silently go stale. Lindy auto-refreshes its knowledge base every 24 hours (https://community.lindy.ai/x/support/htoqrkuf750a/understanding-resync-knowledge-base-action-with-dy), Fin syncs website and Zendesk content (https://fin.ai/train), and Zapier schedules daily/weekly syncs (https://help.zapier.com/hc/en-us/articles/29457465505805). First scope: kick refreshKnowledgeUrls for new URLs after PATCH, re-fetch URLs older than 24h from the hourly cron in small batches, and show 'last synced' plus an error badge in the Knowledge tab.

Priority: high. Effort: S. Compared with Intercom Fin, Zapier Agents, Lindy (plus OpenAI AgentKit as reference for evals/versioning).

title: Agents: Add saved test cases with an LLM judge and rerun them before publishing
description:
Fin offers Simulations where one LLM plays the customer and another judges handoff timing, content used and standards, with a saved regression library rerun after every change (https://fin.ai/testing); Lindy has offline evals with LLM-as-judge scorers over reference tasks (https://docs.lindy.ai/fundamentals/lindy-101/evals); OpenAI AgentKit ships datasets and trace grading (https://openai.com/index/introducing-agentkit/). We only have a manual playground (components/agents/AgentChat.tsx) and per-message thumbs; there is no test table or runner anywhere under lib/agents*. A small team will not trust an agent after editing instructions without a one-click 'did I break anything' check. First scope: an agent_tests table (user message or short script, expected behavior in plain language, expected tool or handoff), a 'Tests' tab that runs all cases through runAgent in dry-run mode, judges with a cheap model and shows pass/fail with the transcript, and 'save as test' from any conversation.

Priority: high. Effort: L. Compared with Intercom Fin, Zapier Agents, Lindy (plus OpenAI AgentKit as reference for evals/versioning).

title: Agents: Make the playground a dry run that simulates write tools instead of executing them
description:
The playground channel runs the same tools as production (lib/agent-tools.ts only relaxes the email check for playground), so testing an SDR agent books real meetings and sends confirmation emails, creates CRM contacts, opens Track issues and enqueues Flow runs. Fin previews and Releases let you try changes in a space separate from what customers see (https://fin.ai/testing), and AgentKit has preview runs (https://openai.com/index/introducing-agentkit/). This makes people afraid to test, which is the opposite of what builds trust. First scope: a 'simulate actions' toggle on by default in the playground that returns realistic fake outputs for crm_upsert_contact, crm_log_note, cal_book_meeting, track_create_issue, run_flow and POST http_request, marked as simulated in the tool call log.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Intercom Fin, Zapier Agents, Lindy (plus OpenAI AgentKit as reference for evals/versioning).

title: Agents: Let owners require teammate approval before specific write actions run
description:
Zapier Agents pauses at approval steps and waits for you to approve or stop, and Human in the Loop lets reviewers approve, decline or edit data before the action proceeds (https://help.zapier.com/hc/en-us/articles/41776074420493); AgentKit has a User approval node (https://openai.com/index/introducing-agentkit/). Our tools are either fully on or off (toolsConfigSchema in lib/agents-config.ts) and execute immediately. Small teams want the agent to draft a Track issue, a CRM update or a Flow run and let a person confirm, especially at the start. First scope: per-tool 'needs approval' flag, a pending_actions table, an in-app notification with approve/edit/reject, and the agent tells the visitor the request is being reviewed; executed result is posted back to the conversation.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Intercom Fin, Zapier Agents, Lindy (plus OpenAI AgentKit as reference for evals/versioning).

title: Agents: Add draft vs published versions with history and one-click rollback
description:
updateAgent in lib/agents.ts writes instructions, tools and guardrails straight to the live row, so every save in the editor goes to production channels instantly and there is no record of what changed. Fin Releases keep changes in a space separate from the customer-facing version until you publish (https://fin.ai/testing), and AgentKit offers full versioning (https://openai.com/index/introducing-agentkit/). Without versions you cannot tie a drop in thumbs-up to an edit or undo a bad prompt quickly. First scope: an agent_versions snapshot on publish, playground and tests run on the draft, a Publish button with a short diff, and a version list with restore; store version id on agent_conversations for later analytics.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Intercom Fin, Zapier Agents, Lindy (plus OpenAI AgentKit as reference for evals/versioning).

title: Agents: Add an analytics tab with resolution, handoff, tool error and topic metrics
description:
Fin reports resolution rate, involvement rate and CX Score per conversation, groups conversations with Topics Explorer and offers Monitors and scorecards (https://fin.ai/pricing, https://fin.ai/capabilities). We only compute conversations in the last 7 days and all-time thumbs totals in listAgents (lib/agents.ts); the editor has no analytics tab (TABS in components/agents/AgentEditor.tsx). A team cannot decide whether to widen the agent's scope without knowing how often it resolves vs hands off and which questions it fails. First scope: a 'Performance' tab with 30-day series of conversations, handoff rate, step_limit rate, tool error rate by tool, thumbs ratio, and top unanswered queries (search_knowledge calls that returned 'no relevant knowledge found'), all from existing tables.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Intercom Fin, Zapier Agents, Lindy (plus OpenAI AgentKit as reference for evals/versioning).

title: Board: Add real-time multiplayer with live cursors and element-level merge
description:
Miro, FigJam and tldraw all treat simultaneous editing with live cursors as the baseline; tldraw ships an open sync layer (https://tldraw.dev/docs/sync) and Excalidraw exposes isCollaborating, collaborators and reconcileElements so hosts can wire it. Today lib/boards.ts states 'Sin multiplayer en tiempo real' and saves replace the whole scene: a second editor gets a 409 and must choose 'keep mine' (overwrites the teammate) or 'reload' (discards own work) in components/board/BoardEditor.tsx. For a small team running a retro or planning session this is the single biggest blocker to using Board instead of Miro. First scope: per-board presence channel (SSE or websocket) broadcasting element deltas and pointer positions, merged client-side with Excalidraw's reconcileElements, keeping the versioned PUT as the persistence path.

Priority: high. Effort: L. Compared with Miro.

title: Board: Merge concurrent edits per element instead of whole-scene 'keep mine' overwrite
description:
Until full multiplayer lands, the conflict path is destructive: keepMine() in components/board/BoardEditor.tsx re-PUTs the entire local scene over the server version, silently deleting anything a teammate added, and 'reload' throws away local work. Miro never asks users to pick a winner, and Excalidraw already exports reconcileElements (present in node_modules/@excalidraw/excalidraw types) to merge two element arrays by id and version. This is a data-loss defect for any team of 2+ editing the same board. First scope: on 409, GET the server scene, reconcile with local elements, updateScene with the merged result and retry the save against the new version, only showing a banner when the merge is ambiguous.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Miro.

title: Board: Fix pending changes lost when leaving the editor during an in-flight save
description:
The unmount effect in components/board/BoardEditor.tsx fires a final PUT with versionRef.current but does not check inFlightRef, so if an autosave is still running it sends the same base version, the first request bumps the version and the final one gets a 409 that nobody sees; the last edits are lost. It also only uses keepalive for bodies under 60 KB and never shows an error. Miro saves continuously with no such window (board history in https://help.miro.com/hc/articles/360021668819 is a safety net, which we also lack). First scope: on unmount, wait for or chain after the in-flight request and use the returned version, and persist unsaved scenes to localStorage so the next open can offer to restore them.

Priority: high. Effort: S. Compared with Miro.

title: Board: Add pinned comment threads with @mentions and resolve
description:
Miro lets anyone pin a comment to a spot or object, @mention teammates, reply in threads and resolve them, with notifications (https://help.miro.com/hc/articles/360017572054); FigJam does the same. Our whiteboard has no comments at all: components/board/BoardEditor.tsx only renders the canvas, name and share popover, and the boards table in lib/schema/migrations.ts has no comment storage (components/board/BoardComments.tsx belongs to the public feedback board). Async review is how small remote teams actually use whiteboards between meetings. First scope: board_comments table with x/y or element id anchor, a comment tool and side panel reusing the Docs mention popover and lib/notifications.ts for @mentions.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Miro.

title: Board: Ship a starter template gallery (retro, brainstorm, user flow, kanban, roadmap)
description:
Miro's free plan includes 7,000+ templates (https://miro.com/pricing/, https://miro.com/templates/) and FigJam includes templates on every plan; a blank canvas is the main reason new teams bounce. Today create() in components/board/BoardList.tsx always POSTs an empty board and lib/boards.ts createBoard inserts scene ''; there is no template concept, although Docs already has lib/docs-templates.ts as a pattern. First scope: 8 to 10 built-in scenes (retro, crazy 8s, impact/effort matrix, user story map, weekly planning, flowchart, org chart, SWOT) stored as JSON in the repo, a 'New from template' picker, and 'Save board as template' for the workspace.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Miro.

title: Board: Add sticky notes as a first-class tool with colors, bulk paste and tags
description:
Miro's core object is the sticky note: one-click colored stickies, bulk mode where each line becomes a sticky, pasting a spreadsheet column as stickies, and tags for grouping (https://help.miro.com/hc/articles/360017572054, https://www.offerzen.com/blog/10-tips-for-getting-started-with-miro); the REST API models sticky notes and tags as distinct item types. We only expose stock Excalidraw shapes in components/board/ExcalidrawCanvas.tsx, so a sticky is a manually styled rectangle plus a bound text with no fixed size, palette or tagging. Workshop workflows (brainstorm, affinity mapping, retros) depend on fast stickies. First scope: a custom toolbar button that inserts a square auto-sizing text container with a 6-color palette, 'paste lines as stickies' laid out in a grid, and tag chips stored in element customData.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Miro.

title: Board: Turn selected stickies into Track issues and show them as live cards
description:
Miro converts up to 50 selected stickies into Jira issues in one action and renders them as synced Jira cards on the board (https://miro.com/marketplace/jira); this is a paid-plan feature that depends on a third-party tracker. We own both sides: lib/track-data.ts exposes createIssue, but Board has no link to Track anywhere (no references to track in components/board or lib/boards.ts). Going from workshop output to tracked work in one click is the clearest suite differentiator for a small team. First scope: context menu 'Create Track issues' on selected text/stickies, choosing project and labels, writing the issue id into element customData and a link back to the board, then rendering a status badge on those elements.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Miro.

title: Cal: Run reminder and workflow cron often enough that 'X minutes before' steps arrive
description:
Calendly Workflows send emails and texts at exact offsets such as 30 minutes before the meeting (https://calendly.com/blog/workflows). Our workflow editor lets hosts pick offsets in minutes (components/calendar/EventTypeEditor.tsx), but the only scheduler is /api/cron/tick at '17 * * * *' in vercel.json, and processDueWorkflowRuns in lib/calendar-workflows.ts silently marks a 'before' step as sent and skips it when the hourly tick lands after the meeting start. In practice a '15 minutes before' reminder is dropped roughly three times out of four, which defeats the main no-show reducer. First scope: move calendar reminders and workflow runs to the existing 5 minute cron (or schedule each email at booking time with the provider's scheduled send), and block offsets shorter than the cron interval in the UI with a clear hint.

Priority: high. Effort: S. Compared with Calendly.

title: Cal: Apply buffers of existing bookings too, so buffer protection is not order dependent
description:
Calendly blocks the buffer around every Calendly meeting, so a 30 minute meeting with 15 minute buffers reserves 60 minutes (https://calendly.com/help/how-to-use-buffers). In lib/calendar.ts the buffer is only added to the candidate slot (applyBuffer in slotsForDay, pickFreeHost and HOST_FREE_SQL), while existing bookings are compared with their raw starts_at/ends_at. With bufferAfter=15, booking 8:30 to 9:00 first and then 9:00 to 9:30 is allowed with zero gap, but the reverse order is blocked. Hosts who rely on buffers for travel or prep get back-to-back meetings depending on who booked first. First scope: store the buffered range (or the buffer minutes) on each booking and expand existing bookings by their own buffers in listBusyRanges and HOST_FREE_SQL, plus a unit test for both orders.

Priority: high. Effort: S. Compared with Calendly.

title: Cal: Add start time increments independent of meeting duration
description:
Calendly lets each event type set how often slots start, for example every 15 or 30 minutes regardless of length (https://calendly.com/help/how-to-fine-tune-your-availability-settings). Our engine in computeDaySlots (lib/calendar.ts) steps by durationMin, so a 45 minute event only offers 9:00, 9:45, 10:30 and a 60 minute event cannot start at 9:30. This produces odd times guests do not expect and wastes availability around existing meetings. First scope: add slotIntervalMin to bookingRules (default = duration, options 5/10/15/20/30/60), use it as the loop step in computeDaySlots, and expose it in the editor Limits section.

Priority: high. Effort: S. Compared with Calendly.

title: Cal: Check conflicts across several calendars and add Microsoft 365 / Outlook
description:
Calendly paid plans connect up to six calendars (Google, Office 365, Outlook, Exchange), let the user toggle which ones to check for conflicts and pick one destination calendar (https://blog.calendly.com/connect-multiple-calendars/). Our lib/google-calendar.ts queries freeBusy only for items [{id: 'primary'}], and there is no Microsoft provider at all. Small teams commonly keep a personal or shared team calendar next to the work one, and many SMB customers live in Microsoft 365, so today they get double booked or cannot use Cal. First scope: list the user's Google calendars and let them select which to check (freeBusy accepts many ids), then add a Microsoft Graph provider through registerBusyProvider plus event creation with the same best-effort pattern.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Calendly.

title: Cal: Offer structured locations (Zoom, Teams, phone, in person) with invitee choice
description:
Calendly has native Zoom and Microsoft Teams location types that generate a unique link per booking, plus phone call and in-person locations, and an event can offer several for the invitee to choose (https://help.calendly.com/hc/en-us/articles/223195508). Our location is a single free-text field (components/calendar/EventTypeEditor.tsx) and the only automation is wantsGoogleMeet() sniffing that text in lib/google-calendar.ts. Teams that sell on Zoom or Teams paste a static room link, and phone-call meetings cannot ask the guest for their number. First scope: replace location with a typed list (google_meet, zoom, teams, phone_host, phone_guest, in_person, custom link), let the guest pick when there are several, and add Zoom OAuth meeting creation first.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Calendly.

title: Cal: Add dropdown, radio, checkbox, multi-line and phone questions, plus invitee guests
description:
Calendly invitee questions support one line, multiple lines, radio buttons, checkboxes, dropdown and phone number, and invitees can add guests to the meeting (https://help.calendly.com/hc/en-us/articles/226893168, https://help.calendly.com/hc/en-us/articles/226766767). Our customField in lib/calendar-schema.ts only allows text, number and boolean, and bookingRules.allowGuests exists in the schema but nothing in the editor, booking page or emails uses it. Qualification questions like company size or budget become free text that cannot be filtered or routed, and the guest's colleague never gets the invite. First scope: add select/radio/checkbox/textarea/phone types with options, add a guests field (up to 10 emails) gated by allowGuests, and send them the .ics and Google attendee entry.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Calendly.

title: Chat: Email unread agent replies to offline visitors and thread email replies back
description:
Intercom delivers an inbox reply by email when the customer has not seen it in the Messenger within a few minutes, and Chatwoot's conversation continuity threads the customer's email reply back into the same chat (https://community.intercom.com/questions/6536, https://chatwoot.com/docs/product/channels/live-chat/conversation-continuity). Today an agent reply is only stored and shown on the next widget poll: app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/messages/route.ts sends no email, and lib/chat-visitor-message.ts only notifies agents. For a small team that answers hours later, the visitor has usually left the page, so the reply is never read. First scope: if a visitor with an email has not read an agent message (read_at null) after 5 minutes, send one email with the reply and a link that reopens the widget; then add inbound reply-by-email via a per-conversation reply-to address.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Intercom.

title: Chat: Localize the embedded widget UI (en/es/pt) instead of hardcoded English
description:
Intercom localizes all Messenger UI to the visitor's browser language for every supported language, with a language_override attribute (https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/180-localize-the-messenger-to-work-with-multiple-languages). Our widget script hardcodes English strings such as 'Type a message…', 'Start chat', 'We're away right now.', 'How would you rate your experience?', 'Search articles…' and the default welcome 'Hi there. How can we help?' in app/api/chat/widget.js/route.ts. This breaks PRODUCT.md's rule of no hardcoded UI strings across en/es/pt, and Latin America is the home market, so most end customers see an English widget on a Spanish site. First scope: move widget strings to the chat messages namespace, pick the locale from navigator.language or a data-locale attribute, and add a widget-level default language setting.

Priority: high. Effort: S. Compared with Intercom.

title: Chat: Search inbox by message content, not only subject, name and email
description:
Intercom Inbox search matches conversations containing the query words and combines with tag, user, assignee and date filters, sorted by relevancy or date (https://www.intercom.com/changes/en/2285-find-the-exact-conversations-you-re-looking-for-with-flexible-search-and-filters-for-inbox). Our listChatConversations in lib/chat-data.ts only applies LIKE to c.subject, v.name and v.email, so searching for an order number, error text or a phrase the customer wrote returns nothing. Finding 'the person who asked about X last week' is a daily support task. First scope: add an EXISTS match on chat_messages.body (including notes for agents) with a snippet of the matching message in the list row, then an FTS index if volume needs it.

Priority: high. Effort: S. Compared with Intercom.

title: Chat: Add agent away status that skips round-robin and optionally reassigns
description:
Intercom teammates set an Away status; round robin excludes away teammates and 'away and reassign' sends their open conversations back to the team inbox, and the June 2026 changelog added availability filters (https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/6512504-round-robin-deep-dive, https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/6522874-manage-teammate-status-in-the-next-gen-inbox). Chatwoot has Online/Busy/Offline plus auto-offline. Our applyAssignmentRules in lib/chat-data.ts sorts all workspace agents by active load with no notion of availability, so a teammate on vacation keeps receiving new chats that breach SLA. First scope: an Away toggle in the inbox header (stored per user), round-robin skips away agents, and an option to unassign their open conversations when going away; reuse the CRM lead-assignment out-of-office flag if possible.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Intercom.

title: CRM: Keep synced emails, enrollments and form history when merging contacts
description:
HubSpot merges keep activities, associations and most property values from both records (https://knowledge.hubspot.com/records/merge-records). Our mergeContacts in lib/crm.ts moves contact_id on crm_emails but never repoints crm_email_contacts, and then deletes the dropped contact, so its rows cascade away (lib/schema/migrations.ts:995) and those emails disappear from the kept contact's timeline, which reads through crm_email_contacts (lib/crm-email.ts:777) and also feeds lead scoring. Sequence enrollments cascade-delete, form submissions lose their contact (ON DELETE SET NULL), property history stays orphaned, and empty fields on the kept contact are not filled from the dropped one. A small team merging a duplicate silently loses its email history. Fix: repoint crm_email_contacts, crm_sequence_enrollments, crm_form_submissions and crm_property_events inside the same transaction, fill blank fields from the dropped record, and add a regression test next to tests/unit/crm.test.ts 'merge de contactos'.

Priority: high. Effort: S. Compared with HubSpot.

title: CRM: Add a recycle bin that restores deleted records and activities for 90 days
description:
HubSpot keeps deleted contacts, companies, deals and activities in a restore tool for 90 days, filterable by date, user or workflow (https://knowledge.hubspot.com/records/restore-deleted-records). We hard-delete: deleteContact and bulkDeleteContacts run DELETE FROM crm_contacts directly (lib/crm.ts:767, :886), there is no deleted_at column on any CRM table (lib/schema/baseline.ts), and cascades wipe associations, emails links and enrollments. One mis-click on bulk delete (up to 500 rows) is unrecoverable for a team without a DBA. First scope: deleted_at on contacts, companies, deals and activities, exclude soft-deleted rows in list/search/report queries, a Settings > Deleted records page with restore, and a daily cron purge after 90 days.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with HubSpot.

title: CRM: Bulk edit any property and reassign owner on contacts, companies and deals
description:
HubSpot's index pages let you select records and edit any property value, assign owners or add to segments in one action (https://knowledge.hubspot.com/records/bulk-edit-records). Our contacts and companies bulk endpoints only accept set_lifecycle and delete (app/api/crm/contacts/bulk/route.ts, app/api/crm/companies/bulk/route.ts), and the deals table bulk bar only offers tags (components/crm/DealsTable.tsx:245). When a rep leaves or territories change, a small team has to reassign owners one by one. First scope: a 'Set property' bulk action (owner, lead status, source, stage, close date and custom fields) on all three tables, recorded in crm_property_events and firing the same workflow triggers as single edits.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with HubSpot.

title: CRM: Track last contacted, last activity and next activity date on every record
description:
HubSpot maintains Last activity date, Last contacted, Next activity date and Number of times contacted automatically on each contact (https://knowledge.hubspot.com/properties/hubspots-default-contact-properties), and Pipedrive builds its workflow around a Next activity date with a warning on deals that have nothing scheduled (https://support.pipedrive.com/en/article/activities). We only compute last_activity_at for deals on the board query (lib/crm.ts:1531); contacts and companies have no such fields, the contacts table columns stop at created (components/crm/ContactsTable.tsx:50-59), and the board card shows no next step. For a small team the daily question is 'who have I not talked to and what is my next step', which we cannot answer from a list. First scope: derived last_contacted_at, last_activity_at, next_activity_at on contacts, companies and deals (updated on activity/email write), sortable and filterable columns, and a 'no next activity' marker on board cards.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with HubSpot.

title: CRM: Show owner and custom fields as sortable columns in record tables
description:
HubSpot index views let you add any property, default or custom, as a column and sort or filter by it, and the 2026 index redesign adds conditional highlighting on top (https://offers.hubspot.com/streamlined-index-views-resource-center). Our column toggle only exposes a fixed set: contacts get name, email, phone, company, lifecycle, lead status, source, score, tags, created (components/crm/ContactsTable.tsx:50-59), with no owner column and no custom fields in ContactsTable or DealsTable, even though the filter builder already supports custom fields (lib/crm.ts:187). Teams that add a 'Plan' or 'Region' field cannot see it in the list without opening each record. First scope: owner column on all three tables plus one column per custom field in ColumnToggle, persisted in saved views, sortable via the existing custom-field SQL expression.

Priority: high. Effort: S. Compared with HubSpot.

title: Docs: Make [[ page links real links instead of inserting the title as plain text
description:
Notion inserts a live page mention when you type [[ or @page, which navigates on click, follows renames and creates a backlink (https://www.notion.com/en-gb/help/create-links-and-backlinks). Our onSelectMention in components/docs/DocsEditor.tsx (around line 1362) deletes the [[query and inserts the escaped text "[Page title] ", so nothing is clickable and the feature map's claim that [[ links another page is not true. For a small team wiki, cross-linking pages is the core navigation pattern, and today every link silently becomes dead text. First scope: insert an anchor via wrapLink with href /app/docs/<id> (or a data-page-id mention element allowed by the sanitizer), render it as a page chip with icon, and resolve the current title on render so renames do not break it.

Priority: high. Effort: S. Compared with Notion.

title: Docs: Move the caret between blocks with Arrow Up/Down
description:
In Notion the arrow keys move freely through the page, crossing block boundaries (https://www.notion.com/help/keyboard-shortcuts). Each of our blocks is its own contentEditable (components/docs/DocsBlockEditor.tsx), and handleKeyDown in components/docs/DocsEditor.tsx only handles ArrowUp/Down inside the slash menu, so the caret gets stuck at the first or last line of a block and the user must reach for the mouse. This hurts every editing session, especially on long notes. First scope: when the caret is on the first visual line (ArrowUp) or last visual line (ArrowDown), or at offset 0 / end for ArrowLeft/Right, focus the neighbouring block and place the caret at the matching x position (lib/docs-caret.ts already has offset helpers); also make Delete at the end of a block merge the next one.

Priority: high. Effort: S. Compared with Notion.

title: Docs: Add image and file blocks with upload, paste and drag and drop
description:
Notion supports /image, /file, /video and /pdf blocks, drag and drop from the desktop, paste of screenshots, resize, captions and alt text, even on the Free plan with a 5 MB per file limit (https://www.notion.com/help/images-files-and-media, https://www.notion.com/pricing). Our block enum in lib/docs-schema.ts has no media type, lib/docs-richtext.ts lists IMG/VIDEO in DROP_TAGS so pasted images vanish, and covers only accept a URL. A team writing specs, how-tos or meeting notes constantly pastes screenshots, so this is the most visible missing primitive. First scope: an image block and a file block (name, size, download) backed by the existing lib/uploads.ts (Vercel Blob or local disk), created from /image, clipboard paste and drop, with caption and width; reuse the same upload for covers.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Notion.

title: Docs: Split pasted Markdown or HTML into real blocks and import .md/.docx files
description:
Notion turns pasted rich content into headings, lists and code blocks, and imports Markdown, CSV, Word, Google Docs, HTML and Confluence exports (https://www.notion.com/help/import-data-into-notion). Our onPaste in components/docs/DocsBlockEditor.tsx sanitizes the clipboard and inserts everything into the current block, with block elements collapsed to newlines, so pasting a README or a Google Doc yields one giant paragraph. Teams migrating from Notion, Google Docs or a repo README hit this on day one, and it blocks adoption. First scope: when the clipboard holds multiple block-level elements or Markdown syntax, parse it (marked is already a dependency) into DocsBlock[] and splice them after the caret; then an Import button that accepts .md/.txt/.html files and a zipped Notion Markdown export, preserving the folder tree as subpages.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Notion.

title: Docs: Search page content, not only titles, and add a Cmd+P page switcher
description:
Notion search covers page bodies and comments, and Cmd+P opens search or jumps to recently viewed pages (https://www.notion.com/help/keyboard-shortcuts); Outline advertises instant full-text search as a headline feature (https://www.getoutline.com/). Our searchDocPages in lib/docs.ts runs title LIKE ? only, and app/api/search/route.ts uses it for Cmd+K, so a phrase written inside a page can never be found. Once a team has more than a few dozen pages, finding 'where did we write the refund policy' is the main daily use of a wiki. First scope: search title plus plain text of content (pagePlainText already exists in lib/docs-help.ts) with a snippet around the match and title hits ranked first; add an FTS index later; add a Docs-local Cmd+P palette that lists recent pages when empty.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Notion.

title: Docs: Inherit sharing from parent pages to their subpages
description:
In Notion subpages take on their parent's permissions unless overridden on a specific subpage (https://www.notion.com/help/sharing-and-permissions). Our getDocAccess in lib/docs.ts reads docs_shares WHERE page_id = ? for the page itself only, so sharing a 'Client onboarding' page with a guest or another team gives them the top page while every subpage returns 404, and the owner has to share each child by hand. This makes sharing a section with a contractor or client practically unusable. First scope: walk ancestors in getDocAccess (bounded, cached per request) and take the highest role found, show 'Inherited from <page>' in ShareDialog.tsx, and let the shared-with-me tree show the child pages under the shared root.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Notion.

title: Docs: Add comment replies, @mentions in comments and notifications
description:
Notion comments support threaded replies, comments on a selected text range, @mentions of people inside comments, and Inbox plus email notifications for mentions and replies (https://www.notion.com/help/comments-mentions-and-reminders). Our docs_comments table (lib/schema/baseline.ts) has no parent or text anchor, CommentsPanel.tsx has no reply or mention support, and app/api/docs/pages/[id]/comments/route.ts creates the comment without notifying anyone, so feedback left on a doc is invisible unless the owner happens to open it. Async review of specs and proposals is the main collaboration loop for a small team. First scope: thread replies under a root comment, @mention picker reusing UserMentionPopover, and notifications (lib/notifications.ts) to the page owner, thread participants and mentioned users; anchor-to-selection can follow.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Notion.

title: Docs: Support nested blocks with Tab indent, toggle lists, toggle headings and callouts
description:
Notion lets you nest any block with Tab / Shift+Tab and offers toggle lists, toggle headings and callouts as basic building blocks (https://www.notion.com/help/keyboard-shortcuts, https://www.notion.com/help/columns-headings-and-dividers, https://developers.notion.com/reference/block). Our DocsBlock model is a flat array with no children or indent level (lib/docs-types.ts, lib/docs-schema.ts) and Tab is not handled in components/docs/DocsEditor.tsx, so sub-bullets and collapsible FAQ sections are impossible. Nested lists are the default way people write meeting notes and outlines. First scope: an indent field (0-4) on list/to-do/paragraph blocks driven by Tab/Shift+Tab, a toggle block with collapsible children rendered from following indented blocks, and a callout block with emoji; carry them through docs-markdown export and the help center renderer.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Notion.

title: Flow: Run the scheduler every minute so minute schedules, delays and retries fire on time
description:
Zapier polls every 15 minutes on Free and every 2 minutes on paid plans, and n8n schedules run to the minute (https://zapier.com/pricing). Our editor offers interval schedules in minutes (minimum 5) and Delay in seconds or minutes, but on cloud the Flow queue only drains in the hourly /api/cron/tick ('17 * * * *' in vercel.json); the copy itself admits runs can start up to an hour late (messages/en/flow.json scheduleGranularity and delayGranularity). Node retries schedule jobs 15 s to 1 h out and also wait for the next tick. This silently breaks the most common small-team automation, 'every 15 minutes check X', and any follow-up delay. First scope: call processFlowQueue from the existing 5-minute /api/cron/robots route (or add a 1-minute cron for Flow only), then remove the granularity warnings.

Priority: high. Effort: S. Compared with Zapier / n8n.

title: Flow: Add actions to update CRM records, create tasks and update Track issues
description:
Zapier and n8n app nodes cover create, update, get and search for every object (for example the n8n HubSpot node: contacts, deals, tasks, engagements, https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/app-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.hubspot/). Flow can only create a contact (an existing email returns created:false without updating fields), enroll in a sequence, list deals created in the last N hours, and create a Track issue (lib/flow-engine.ts crmContactNode, crmDealsNode, trackIssueNode). There is no update contact, find contact, create or update deal, move deal stage, create CRM task or note, update issue status or assignee, or create a Cal booking link, even though CRM workflows already implement update_field and create_task (lib/crm-workflow-catalog.ts). Cross-app automation is the reason to use Flow instead of Zapier, so these are table stakes. First scope: app.crm_contact upsert plus app.crm_deal (create/update/move stage), app.crm_task and app.track_issue update, with pickers instead of raw IDs for projectId, sequenceId and robotId.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Zapier / n8n.

title: Flow: Add date and text formatter filters (format, add time, timezone, replace, split)
description:
Zapier Formatter is used in a large share of Zaps: date format, add or subtract time (+1 day -2 hours), timezone conversion, text replace, split, truncate, number formatting (https://help.zapier.com/hc/en-us/articles/31162113958925). n8n exposes Luxon date helpers and string helpers in every expression. Our template engine has 13 filters and {{now}} only as an ISO string, with no date formatting, date math, replace, split, slice or round (lib/flow-template.ts applyFilter), and unknown filters are silently ignored. Without this, users fall back to the Code step, which needs Vercel Sandbox and is unavailable on many self-hosts. First scope: add date:'format':tz, add:'+1d', replace, split, slice, round and fail validation on unknown filter names.

Priority: high. Effort: S. Compared with Zapier / n8n.

title: Flow: Let webhooks reply with custom data and accept GET and header or basic auth
description:
n8n's Webhook node accepts GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE and HEAD, supports basic, header and JWT auth, and can respond when the last node finishes or through a Respond to Webhook node with custom status, headers and body (https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.webhook/, https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.respondtowebhook/). Our hook route only exports POST and always answers 202 {runId} before the flow runs (app/api/flow/hooks/[token]/route.ts). That blocks verification handshakes (Meta/WhatsApp hub.challenge, Slack url_verification), form handlers that need a redirect, and small APIs built on Flow. First scope: GET support, an optional shared-secret header check, and a 'Respond to webhook' node that waits up to about 10 s for a synchronous answer.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Zapier / n8n.

title: Flow: Add an approval step that pauses a run until someone approves in Slack or email
description:
Zapier Human in the Loop pauses a Zap until reviewers approve, decline or edit data, notified by email or Slack, with a Decision field for branching (https://help.zapier.com/hc/en-us/articles/38733184458765/). n8n ships 'Send and wait for response' on Slack, Gmail, Telegram, WhatsApp and more, and human review for AI agent tools (https://docs.n8n.io/advanced-ai/human-in-the-loop-tools/). Flow already has a waiting state and resumable jobs (lib/flow-engine.ts result.kind 'wait', resumeRun) but only Delay uses it. For small teams this is the safe way to let AI draft a reply or a quote and have a human click approve before it goes out. First scope: a logic.approval node with approved/rejected/timeout outputs, notifying by email and Slack with signed links, plus an approvals inbox in the Flow app.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Zapier / n8n.

title: Flow: Add workspace data tables for lookups, dedupe and state between runs
description:
Zapier Tables is included on Free (2,500 records, table steps do not count as tasks) and n8n added Data tables with a Data Table node, CSV import and an API, used to store markers that prevent duplicate runs and lookup lists (https://zapier.com/pricing, https://docs.n8n.io/data/data-tables/). Flow has no persistent storage: every run only sees its trigger and node outputs (lib/flow-engine.ts templateCtx), so 'only notify once per contact', counters, or a mapping table need an external Google Sheet. First scope: a flow_tables store per workspace (simple typed columns, 10k rows), a data.table node with insert, upsert by key, find and delete, and a small table view in the Flow app.

Priority: high. Effort: L. Compared with Zapier / n8n.

title: Flow: Add triggers for Notes, Board, Agents and task, chat and booking lifecycles
description:
Zapier and n8n triggers exist for nearly every record change in an app (new or updated item, status change). Our event bus (lib/events.ts) is called from Cal, Link, CRM, Track, Chat, Docs and Robots, but Notes, Board and Agents emit nothing, so 3 of our 11 apps cannot start a flow (no emitEvent in lib/agents.ts, notes or board code). Useful events also missing: crm task due or completed (CRM workflows have task_due), chat conversation closed or assigned, agent handoff to a human, booking no-show, docs page updated, issue assigned. Triggering across our own apps is the core promise of Flow. First scope: board.card_created/moved, agent.handoff, conversation.closed, task.due and page.updated, each with an EVENT_SAMPLES entry.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Zapier / n8n.

title: Link: Forward query parameters from the short link to the destination URL
description:
Dub appends any query string on the short link (for example ?utm_source=newsletter) to the destination, with the short link value winning on conflicts, so one link can be reused across channels (https://dub.co/help/article/parameter-passing). Our middleware already forwards req.nextUrl.search into /r/<slug>, but app/r/[slug]/route.ts redirects to link.url or the targeting destination and drops every incoming param except reading ?qr=1. Marketers who tag a short link per channel silently lose that attribution today. First scope: merge incoming params into the resolved destination (strip our internal qr param), apply to deep link fallbacks too, and add a per-link toggle defaulting to on.

Priority: high. Effort: S. Compared with Bitly / Dub.

title: Link: Track leads and sales per link and attribute them to CRM contacts and deals
description:
Dub Conversions records lead and sale events against the click that produced them (client SDK plus /track/lead and /track/sale, Stripe integration) and shows clicks to leads to sales funnels per link (https://dub.co/help/article/dub-conversions, https://dub.co/docs/integrations/stripe). We only record clicks (lib/track.ts recordClick); there is no click id, no conversion table and no lead/sale event. We already own a CRM, so this is a strong differentiator: a click id cookie on redirect, a lightweight track endpoint, and CRM form submissions or deal won events attributed back to the originating link. First scope: set a zs_click id on redirect, accept POST /api/v1/track/lead with that id, and show leads per link in analytics and on the CRM contact timeline.

Priority: high. Effort: L. Compared with Bitly / Dub.

title: Link: Add filters (tag, domain, link, country, device) and timezone to analytics
description:
Dub analytics can filter and group by tag, folder, domain, link, country, region, city, device, browser, OS, referrer URL and UTM values, with an IANA timezone for day buckets (https://dub.co/docs/api-reference/endpoint/retrieve-analytics). Our workspace dashboard in lib/link-analytics.ts takes only a date range and the per-link view in lib/track.ts getAnalytics only a preset range; both bucket days in UTC and the workspace view omits OS. A small team running a campaign cannot answer 'how did links tagged launch perform in Brazil on mobile'. First scope: tag, domain, country and device filters on the workspace dashboard and API, OS breakdown, and day buckets in the workspace timezone.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Bitly / Dub.

title: Link: Let expired and missing links redirect to a custom URL per link and domain
description:
Dub supports expiredUrl per link and expiredUrl/notFoundUrl defaults per domain, so a dead campaign link lands on a useful page instead of an error (https://dub.co/help/article/link-expiration, https://dub.co/help/article/setting-not-found-url). In app/r/[slug]/route.ts every expired, limit-reached, archived or unknown slug goes to the zerosoft /gone page, even on a customer's own branded domain; link_domains only has root_url. Printed QR codes and old campaign emails keep getting traffic long after expiry, and a zerosoft error page on a customer domain looks broken. First scope: expired_url column on links, expired_url and not_found_url on link_domains, used by the gone() branches.

Priority: high. Effort: S. Compared with Bitly / Dub.

title: Notes: Preserve the clip and deep link through sign-in instead of dropping them
description:
Evernote's Web Clipper prompts sign-in and then completes the clip (https://help.evernote.com/hc/en-us/articles/209125827). Our clip page and the main Notes page call requireUser, which redirects to /auth/signin without a callbackUrl (lib/session.ts requireUser), even though the sign-in page already supports ?callbackUrl= (app/[locale]/auth/signin/page.tsx). A logged-out user who clicks the bookmarklet loses the URL, title and selection, and anyone opening a shared ?note=<id> link lands on the generic app home. This silently breaks the main capture path on any new device or expired session. First scope: let requireUser accept the current path plus query and pass it as callbackUrl, starting with /app/notes/clip and /app/notes.

Priority: high. Effort: S. Compared with Evernote.

title: Notes: Add image and file attachments with drag, drop and paste into a note
description:
Evernote treats attachments (images, PDFs, audio, any file) as first-class note content, and its 2026 releases added image annotation, a PDF editor, image resizing in tables and attachment printing (https://releasebot.io/updates/evernote). Our notes can only hold text blocks: DocsBlockType has no image or file type (lib/docs-types.ts) and there is no upload route under app/api/notes, although lib/uploads.ts already powers attachments in Track, Chat and CRM tasks. Without attachments users cannot save receipts, whiteboard photos, screenshots or contracts, which is the core everyday use of a notes app. First scope: an image block and a file block in the Notes editor, upload via paste, drop and a button using lib/uploads.ts, rendered in the editor, the trash view and the public share page.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Evernote.

title: Notes: Add reminders with date and time that notify in-app and by email
description:
Evernote lets you set a reminder on any note with a date and time, lists reminders at the top of the note list and can send email alerts (https://help.evernote.com/hc/articles/208314338); Google Keep adds time and location reminders synced to every device (https://9to5google.com/2023/01/31/what-you-can-do-google-keep/). Our note schema has no reminder or due field (lib/notes-schema.ts, lib/notes-types.ts NoteSummary) and Notes never touches lib/notifications.ts or the cron jobs. Reminders turn a passive note into a follow-up and are table stakes in every competitor's free tier. First scope: one reminder_at per note, a bell button in the note bar, a Reminders section in the nav, and a cron that sends an in-app notification plus an email when due.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Evernote.

title: Notes: Include notes in the global Cmd+K search results
description:
Evernote search is the front door to the app and spans titles, text and even attachments (https://help.evernote.com/hc/articles/208313828). Our suite-wide search route only queries CRM, Links, Docs and tasks (app/api/search/route.ts) even though lib/notes.ts already has a fast FTS5 search per person. Users who live in other zerosoft apps cannot find a note without first opening Notes, which undercuts the 'one suite' value. First scope: add a notes group to /api/search using listNotes with q and a small limit, scoped to the current person, linking to /app/notes?note=<id>.

Priority: high. Effort: S. Compared with Evernote.

title: Notes: Detect edit conflicts between tabs or devices instead of last write wins
description:
Evernote keeps note history and creates conflicting-change copies so that edits from two devices are never silently lost (https://help.evernote.com/hc/articles/208313858). Our autosave PATCH sends the whole title and block array with no version or updated_at precondition (components/notes/NotesApp.tsx saveContent, lib/notes.ts updateNote), so a stale tab or a laptop left open overwrites newer content written on a phone. PATCH also accepts content edits on trashed notes. This is silent data loss in the most common multi-device scenario. First scope: send the last known updated_at with each save, return 409 when the server row is newer, and show a 'This note changed elsewhere, reload or keep mine' banner; reject content edits on trashed notes.

Priority: high. Effort: S. Compared with Evernote.

title: Robots: Queue runs instead of failing as busy when another workspace run is active
description:
UiPath Orchestrator queues pending jobs per robot and only raises an alert when a trigger cannot create jobs (https://docs.uipath.com/orchestrator/standalone/2023.4/user-guide/alerts), and Browse AI queues tasks for bulk runs (https://www.browse.ai/monitoring). Our startRobotRun inserts a run only when no other run in the workspace is running, otherwise returns busy (lib/robots.ts). For schedules, runDueRobots advances next_run_at before starting, so a collision with a manual or Flow run records a failed busy run and that scheduled execution is lost; from Flow, app.robot_run fails unless the node has retries (default 0, lib/flow-engine.ts robotNode). Teams with two or three robots will see random failures they did not cause, which destroys trust. First scope: add a queued status, insert as queued when busy, and drain the queue in /api/cron/robots and after each run finishes, with a max queue age.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with UiPath (StudioX, Autopilot, Orchestrator, Healing Agent), Browse AI, Axiom.ai, Bardeen, Browserbase/Stagehand, Skyvern.

title: Robots: Send failure alerts and auto-pause schedules after N consecutive failures
description:
Axiom.ai notifies by email or webhook when a run fails, succeeds, or succeeds with warnings (https://axiom.ai/docs/troubleshooting/error-handling), and UiPath Orchestrator sends Error alerts for failed jobs and disables a trigger after its job fails five times in a row (https://docs.uipath.com/orchestrator/standalone/2023.4/user-guide/alerts). We only emit robot.run.failed (lib/robots.ts); there is no in-app or email notification unless the user builds a Flow, and lib/notifications.ts has no robot hook. A scheduled robot that silently fails for a week is the top reason people stop trusting RPA. First scope: per-robot setting 'notify on failure' (creator and admins, in-app plus email, digest at most once per hour) and an auto-pause after 5 consecutive scheduled failures with a banner in RobotsHome.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with UiPath (StudioX, Autopilot, Orchestrator, Healing Agent), Browse AI, Axiom.ai, Bardeen, Browserbase/Stagehand, Skyvern.

title: Robots: Capture a screenshot, URL and DOM snippet automatically when a step fails
description:
Browserbase records every session as video with a Session Inspector and live debug URL so failures can be replayed (https://docs.browserbase.com/features/session-recording, https://docs.browserbase.com/features/session-debugger). Our interpreter only takes screenshots when the robot has an explicit screenshot step; on a failed step it logs a code like s3: action_timeout plus the first line of the Playwright message (lib/robots-interpreter.ts runList). Without seeing the page at the moment of failure (cookie banner, login wall, changed layout) users cannot fix a robot. First scope: in the catch of runList, take one failure screenshot (outside the 5-shot cap), record page.url() and the outerHTML of the nearest match or body excerpt, and show them next to the failed log row in RunsPanel.

Priority: high. Effort: S. Compared with UiPath (StudioX, Autopilot, Orchestrator, Healing Agent), Browse AI, Axiom.ai, Bardeen, Browserbase/Stagehand, Skyvern.

title: Robots: Record fallback selectors per step and self-heal when the primary one breaks
description:
UiPath Unified Target keeps several targeting strategies and the Healing Agent votes on a candidate selector when one is not found, recommending or applying fixes (https://docs.uipath.com/agents/automation-cloud/latest/user-guide-ha/what-is-healing-agent); Browse AI says it detects layout changes and adapts the robot, notifying the user (https://help.browse.ai/en/articles/10486935-how-browse-ai-uses-ai); Stagehand re-infers a selector when a cached one stops resolving (https://docs.stagehand.dev/v4/best-practices/caching). Our recorder computes candidates but keeps only the first unique one (generateSelector in lib/robots-recorder.ts), and resolveTarget tries one selector and then visible text (lib/robots-interpreter.ts). Selector rot is the main maintenance cost of browser robots. First scope: store a fallbacks array (testid, aria-label, name, text, CSS path) per step from the recorder, try them in order at runtime, log 'healed via fallback N', and offer a one-click 'promote fallback' in the run view.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with UiPath (StudioX, Autopilot, Orchestrator, Healing Agent), Browse AI, Axiom.ai, Bardeen, Browserbase/Stagehand, Skyvern.

title: Robots: Add an extract_list step that turns repeating cards into rows with named fields
description:
Browse AI 'capture list' and Bardeen scrapers extract repeating items (product cards, search results, directory entries) into rows with columns the user names (https://help.browse.ai/en/articles/10486935-how-browse-ai-uses-ai, https://www.bardeen.ai/pricing), and Stagehand extract() returns typed data validated against a schema (https://docs.stagehand.dev/). We have extract_table, which only works on HTML <table>, and extract mode all, which returns a flat array of texts for one selector (lib/robots-interpreter.ts). Most real scraping targets (listings, leads, prices) are div-based lists, so today users must write an evaluate step in JS. First scope: extract_list with an item selector plus up to 20 fields (name, relative selector, text or attribute), capped at 500 rows, rendered by the existing table view in RunsPanel.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with UiPath (StudioX, Autopilot, Orchestrator, Healing Agent), Browse AI, Axiom.ai, Bardeen, Browserbase/Stagehand, Skyvern.

title: Robots: Add pagination that clicks Next until missing and appends rows across pages
description:
Axiom.ai has a Find pager setting and a scrape API that keeps paginating until max results or the pager selector stops matching (https://axiom.ai/scrape/multiple-pages/, https://axiom.ai/docs/developer-hub/api/step-functions/scrape/). Our only loop is loop_over over a known list, nested loops are rejected, and if_exists can only jump forward (lib/robots-schema.ts validateSteps), so a 'repeat until there is no Next button' pattern is impossible. Multi-page results are the default for directories, marketplaces and admin panels. First scope: a paginate option on extract_table and extract_list (next selector, max pages up to 20, wait after click) that concatenates rows into the same variable, counted against MAX_PAGES and MAX_EXECUTED_STEPS.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with UiPath (StudioX, Autopilot, Orchestrator, Healing Agent), Browse AI, Axiom.ai, Bardeen, Browserbase/Stagehand, Skyvern.

title: Track: Let authors edit and delete their own issue comments
description:
Linear lets you edit or delete your own comment from its overflow menu and resolve threads (https://linear.app/docs/comment-on-issues). In Track, app/api/track/issues/[id]/comments/route.ts only exposes GET and POST; deleteIssueComment in lib/track-data.ts is never called, and the comment body is also copied into the activity meta, so a typo or a leaked secret stays forever. commentCreateSchema (lib/track-schema.ts) also has no min length, so the API accepts empty comments even though the UI disables the button. First scope: PATCH and DELETE on /api/track/issues/[id]/comments/[commentId] restricted to the author, render the comment from track_issue_comments instead of activity meta, show an edited marker, and require body min(1).

Priority: high. Effort: S. Compared with Linear.

title: Track: Add a Markdown rich text editor for issue descriptions and comments
description:
Linear's editor converts typed or pasted Markdown into rich text, supports code blocks, attachments via /file and links @ENG-123 mentions as related issues (https://linear.app/docs/editor). Track stores descriptions as a single text block edited in a plain textarea (components/track/IssueDetailClient.tsx parseDescription, track-description-input), and comments are plain text. Bug reports and specs need headings, lists, code and inline images to be readable. First scope: reuse the Docs editor or a lightweight Markdown renderer for descriptions and comments, with code blocks, lists, links and pasted images uploaded as attachments; auto-link SLUG-N references.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Linear.

title: Track: Let users subscribe to issues and notify all subscribers on changes
description:
Linear auto-subscribes creators, assignees and mentioned users, allows manual subscribe/unsubscribe (Shift+S) and notifies every subscriber (https://linear.app/docs/notifications). Track hardcodes recipients: status changes go to assignee and creator, comments to mentions, assignee and creator (lib/notifications.ts, lib/track-data.ts createIssueComment), with no subscriber table. A reviewer or stakeholder who wants to follow an issue has no way to do it, and the creator cannot opt out. First scope: track_issue_subscribers table, auto-subscribe on create, assign, mention and comment, a Subscribe toggle on the issue page, and route all Track notifications through it.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Linear.

title: Track: Send email notifications and a daily digest for Track activity
description:
Linear delivers notifications by desktop, mobile, Slack and urgency-timed email digests, configurable per type (https://linear.app/docs/notifications). Track notifications only exist in the in-app inbox (components/track/InboxClient.tsx, lib/notifications.ts has no email path for track types), so anyone not looking at the app misses assignments and mentions. For small teams that live in email, this is the main reason issues go stale. First scope: per-user setting for immediate email on assigned and mention, plus an optional daily digest of unread Track notifications, sent with the existing system sender.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Linear.

title: Track: Expose issues, projects and comments in the public /api/v1 with webhooks
description:
Linear's public GraphQL API covers issues, projects, cycles, labels, comments and relations, plus webhooks for every entity (https://linear.app/developers, https://linear.app/developers/webhooks). Our public API (app/api/v1) covers agents, calendar, crm and links but has no track resource; app/api/track/* only accepts session auth. Teams cannot script imports, sync with other tools, or let CI open issues. First scope: /api/v1/track/issues (list, get, create, update), projects and comments, with API key scopes from lib/api-auth.ts and entries in openapi.json; reuse the generic webhooks table for issue.created and issue.updated.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Linear.

title: Track: Create cycles automatically on a cadence and roll over unfinished issues
description:
Linear creates upcoming cycles automatically with a 1 to 8 week length and start day, auto-adds started issues to the current cycle, rolls unfinished issues forward and keeps a scope/progress graph per cycle (https://linear.app/docs/use-cycles). Track cycles are created one by one by hand (cycleCreateSchema in lib/track-schema.ts, components/track/CyclesPanel.tsx) and rollover only happens when someone clicks Complete. Teams forget to create the next sprint and the overview shows No cycle. First scope: per-project cycle settings (length, start weekday, how many upcoming), a daily cron that creates future cycles and completes ended ones with rollover, and estimate-based progress in CyclesPanel.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Linear.

title: Agents: Turn unanswered questions into suggested Docs pages the team can approve
description:
Fin reviews real conversations to recommend content updates and surface missing topics, approvable in one click from its Optimize dashboard (https://fin.ai/train, https://fin.ai/capabilities). We already log every search_knowledge call with its query and empty results in agent_tool_calls and have Docs in the same suite, but nothing connects them (lib/agent-tools.ts, lib/agents.ts). This is a suite advantage: the fix lands directly in the knowledge source the agent reads live. First scope: weekly job that clusters empty-result queries plus handoff reasons, drafts an answer from the teammate replies in handed-off Chat conversations, and creates an unpublished Docs page linked to the agent for review.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Intercom Fin, Zapier Agents, Lindy (plus OpenAI AgentKit as reference for evals/versioning).

title: Agents: Give the agent the identified visitor's CRM, Cal and Track context
description:
Fin personalizes answers using customer data and connectors (Stripe, Shopify, Salesforce) and can route by customer attributes (https://fin.ai/capabilities, https://fin.ai/train). Our prompt (buildAgentInstructions in lib/agents.ts) contains no visitor identity even when the Chat widget already knows the visitor's email, and the agent can only learn a contact's first name and lifecycle stage via crm_find_contact (lib/agent-tools.ts). Owning CRM, Cal and Track lets us do this without integrations: upcoming bookings, open issues the visitor reported, deal stage. First scope: when the Chat visitor has a verified email, inject a short read-only context block (name, company, lifecycle stage, next booking, open Track issues by that email) and add tools to list or cancel that visitor's own bookings.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Intercom Fin, Zapier Agents, Lindy (plus OpenAI AgentKit as reference for evals/versioning).

title: Agents: Add semantic retrieval and show source links in answers
description:
Our search is in-memory BM25 over keyword tokens with a small ES/EN/PT stopword list (lib/knowledge-search.ts), so a question phrased differently from the doc, or in another language than the doc, often returns nothing and triggers a handoff. Fin answers in 45+ languages from the same content (https://fin.ai/capabilities). search_knowledge already returns a source for URLs but the visitor never sees which page an answer came from, which hurts trust and makes wrong answers hard to debug. First scope: hybrid ranking (BM25 plus embeddings via the AI Gateway, cached per chunk with a content hash), and an instruction plus UI to append one source link (Docs public URL or web URL) to answers that used knowledge.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Intercom Fin, Zapier Agents, Lindy (plus OpenAI AgentKit as reference for evals/versioning).

title: Agents: Alert the owner when thumbs-down, tool errors or step limits spike
description:
Fin Monitors evaluate live conversations against standards you define and alert when a threshold is crossed (https://fin.ai/testing, https://fin.ai/pricing). We record ratings in agent_feedback, tool errors in agent_tool_calls and the step_limit status in runAgent (lib/agents.ts), but only handoffs produce a notification (lib/agent-tools.ts). A small team will not watch a dashboard daily; a push when something breaks (for example a Cal event type deactivated making every booking fail) is what keeps an agent safe to leave running. First scope: hourly cron check per agent for tool error rate, thumbs-down count and step_limit count over the last 24h vs threshold, sending one in-app and email notification with a link to the failing conversations.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with Intercom Fin, Zapier Agents, Lindy (plus OpenAI AgentKit as reference for evals/versioning).

title: Agents: Answer email threads from CRM inboxes as a channel, draft-first
description:
Fin deploys to email, WhatsApp, SMS, Slack and voice (https://fin.ai/pricing), and Lindy drafts and triages email (https://docs.lindy.ai/features/inbox-management/email-drafting.md). Our channels are the Chat widget, the public page, the API and the Flow node (AgentChannel in lib/agents-config.ts, lib/agents-chat.ts); there is no email channel even though the suite already handles email in lib/crm-email.ts. Email is where most small-team support and sales actually happens. First scope: assign an agent to a CRM email inbox in 'draft' mode, where it writes a reply draft on each inbound thread for a teammate to send, with the same tools and logging as other channels.

Priority: medium. Effort: L. Compared with Intercom Fin, Zapier Agents, Lindy (plus OpenAI AgentKit as reference for evals/versioning).

title: Board: Add voting sessions and a shared timer for workshops
description:
Miro puts voting (set a voting area, N votes per person, reveal results) and a timer visible to everyone in its facilitation toolbar, included from the Starter plan (https://miro.com/pricing/, https://help.miro.com/hc/articles/360017572274); FigJam lists timer and voting too. Our board has neither: components/board/BoardEditor.tsx has no facilitation controls and there is no realtime channel to broadcast a timer. Dot voting and timeboxing are what make a retro or prioritization session work for a 5-person team. First scope: a facilitator panel to start a vote over selected elements with a per-person vote budget, tallies shown as badges, and a countdown timer stored on the board row and polled by participants until multiplayer exists.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Miro.

title: Board: Store pasted images in blob storage instead of inline base64 in the scene
description:
Miro and FigJam handle boards full of screenshots without size errors. We keep every image as a dataURL inside the scene JSON (buildScene in components/board/BoardEditor.tsx keeps files inline) under a 4 MB cap (lib/boards-types.ts BOARD_MAX_SCENE_BYTES), so a handful of screenshots triggers the 'too large' block and stops saving, and every autosave re-uploads all images. lib/uploads.ts already provides Vercel Blob or local disk storage for Chat and Track attachments. First scope: on new file, upload it via lib/uploads.ts, replace dataURL with the blob URL in the files map, and lazy-load files on open, keeping the inline path as fallback for self-host without a token.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Miro.

title: Board: Embed live boards in Docs pages with a /board block
description:
Miro boards embed live in Notion and Confluence with pan and zoom, synced as the board changes (https://www.miro.com/marketplace/notion-embed). Our Docs block types in lib/docs-types.ts stop at paragraph through database with no embed, and the only way to show a board elsewhere is the public /b/<token> page (app/[locale]/b/[token]/page.tsx), which would expose it to everyone. Specs, PRDs and meeting notes in Docs routinely need the diagram next to the text. First scope: a 'board' Docs block that picks a workspace board and renders BoardViewer read-only with an 'Open in Board' link, authorized by workspace session rather than a public token.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Miro.

title: Board: Add board version history with hourly snapshots and restore as copy
description:
Miro backs up boards hourly and at the end of each session, keeps versions for 90 days and restores a version as a separate board (https://help.miro.com/hc/articles/360021668819). We store only the latest scene in the boards row (lib/schema/migrations.ts) and saveBoardScene in lib/boards.ts overwrites it, so an accidental delete-all or a 'keep mine' overwrite is unrecoverable; Docs already has lib/docs-versions.ts. First scope: write a board_versions snapshot at most once per hour per board on save, list them in a side panel with editor and time, and restore into a new board via the existing duplicate path.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Miro.

title: Board: Add guest edit links and per-board access instead of workspace-wide only
description:
Miro Starter lets public boards be edited without sign-in and supports private boards with explicit access control (https://miro.com/pricing/). We have two states only: every workspace member can edit every board (lib/boards.ts header comment and listBoards by workspace_id), and the public token is strictly view-only (BoardViewer viewMode in app/[locale]/b/[token]/page.tsx). Small teams often run workshops with clients or freelancers who are not workspace members, and sometimes need a private draft board. First scope: share popover options 'Anyone with link can view / can edit' with an edit token routed to the editor, plus a 'Private to me' flag filtered in listBoards.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Miro.

title: Board: Persist the shape library and enable installing libraries from Excalidraw's catalog
description:
Miro and FigJam keep team asset libraries (FigJam Professional 'Team libraries', https://www.figma.com/figjam/jamboard-alternative/), and Excalidraw+ sells persistent team libraries. Our ExcalidrawCanvas in components/board/ExcalidrawCanvas.tsx passes no onLibraryChange, libraryReturnUrl or useHandleLibrary adapter (all exported by @excalidraw/excalidraw 0.18), so items a user adds to the library vanish on reload and 'Browse libraries' cannot import back into the app. This is a visible defect in a feature the UI already advertises. First scope: useHandleLibrary with a workspace-scoped adapter stored in a board_libraries row, and libraryReturnUrl pointing to the current board so #addLibrary imports work.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with Miro.

title: Cal: Add daily, weekly and monthly meeting limits per event type and per host
description:
Calendly lets an event type cap bookings per day, week or month, and also caps total meetings across all event types; whichever limit hits first removes availability (https://calendly.com/help/how-to-set-meeting-limits). Our bookingRules in lib/calendar-schema.ts only have buffers, notice and horizon, and loadSlotContext in lib/calendar.ts has no count check. Founders and solo sellers use limits to protect focus time, for example at most 3 demos a day. First scope: add maxPerDay and maxPerWeek to bookingRules, count confirmed and pending bookings per host in the slot engine, and enforce it again inside the booking INSERT.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Calendly.

title: Cal: Create collective event types where every selected host must be free
description:
Calendly Collective events let several teammates meet one invitee and only show times when all hosts are available, and shared collective events are on Standard (https://calendly.com/help/how-to-set-up-a-shared-collective-event-type). We only have round-robin: candidateHosts and busyForHosts in lib/calendar.ts accept a slot if at least one host is free. Small teams constantly need 'founder plus engineer' demos or 'two partners' consults. First scope: add a hostMode (round_robin | collective) on the event type, intersect free time across hosts in slotsForDay, book all hosts in one transaction, and add every host as an attendee on the Google event.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Calendly.

title: Cal: Redirect invitees after booking and capture UTM parameters on the booking
description:
Calendly can redirect to an external URL after booking and optionally append event name, invitee name, email and UTM tags, available from Standard (https://calendly.com/help/how-to-redirect-invitees-to-another-site-after-booking). Our booking page only redirects to Stripe Checkout (components/calendar/PublicBookingPage.tsx) and the page route reads just name and email from the query (app/[locale]/book/[handle]/[slug]/page.tsx); bookings store no source or UTM. Marketers cannot fire a thank-you page conversion pixel or attribute demos to campaigns, which also weakens the CRM sync. First scope: per-event redirectUrl with a 'pass details' toggle, persist utm_* and referrer on calendar_bookings, and include them in webhooks and the CRM activity.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with Calendly.

title: Cal: Add one-off meetings that offer hand-picked times outside normal availability
description:
Calendly one-off meetings let the host pick specific slots on a calendar, including over non-Calendly events or outside working hours, then share a link or paste the times into an email; Meeting Polls extend this with voting (https://help.calendly.com/hc/en-us/articles/4406031977623, https://help.calendly.com/hc/en-us/articles/4411543910551). We have single-use links (singleUse in lib/calendar.ts) but they still use the event's regular schedule, so a host cannot offer 'Tuesday 18:00 or Thursday 8:00' to one VIP. This is one of the most common daily actions for sellers and founders. First scope: a 'Share specific times' dialog that creates a hidden single-use event type with explicit slot overrides and a copy-as-text option; polls can follow later.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Calendly.

title: Cal: Ship a booking analytics view with created, cancelled, no-show and popular times
description:
Calendly Analytics shows created, completed, rescheduled and canceled events, popular event types and popular times for up to a year, filterable by user and event type, on Standard and up (https://calendly.com/help/calendly-analytics). Our Cal overview (app/[locale]/app/calendar/page.tsx) only shows an upcoming-7-days count and the next five bookings. Without trends a small team cannot see no-show rate, which rep gets demos, or which hours to open. First scope: a stats tab over calendar_bookings for a date range with counts by status, by event type and host, cancellation and no-show rates, and a weekday by hour heatmap.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Calendly.

title: Cal: Let routing forms end in a URL or message, log submissions and pass answers on
description:
Calendly routing forms can send respondents to an event type, a custom message or an external URL, and emit routing_form_submission.created webhooks (https://community.calendly.com/featured-tips-tricks-32/12-days-of-calendly-day-10-routing-for-teams-527, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/calendlyv2). Our evaluateRouting in lib/calendar-routing.ts can only return an event type slug, rules have a single condition, submissions are not stored, and only name and email reach the booking (components/calendar/PublicRoutingForm.tsx). Disqualified leads hit a dead end and the host never sees the qualification answers. First scope: destination types (event, url, message), a submissions table visible in the form editor, carry all answers into booking answers, and a routing.submitted event for webhooks and Flow.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Calendly.

title: Cal: Add an optional host approval step (requires confirmation) for bookings
description:
Cal.com event types can require the host to accept each booking, always or only when booked within a notice window (https://cal.com/help/event-types/how-to-requires). Our bookings are confirmed instantly; the only pending state is the Stripe hold in lib/calendar.ts createBooking. Consultants, agencies and clinics want to screen requests before committing the slot. First scope: a requiresConfirmation flag that creates a pending booking holding the slot, host emails with Accept/Decline links and an admin action in BookingsList, guest notified either way, and a booking.requested webhook.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Calendly.

title: Chat: Bulk select conversations in the inbox to assign, tag, snooze or resolve
description:
Intercom's Inbox has checkboxes and an action bar to bulk assign, close, snooze, tag and set priority, including from search results (https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/6274899-get-started-with-intercom-inbox). Our inbox list in components/chat/ConversationList.tsx and components/chat/InboxShell.tsx has no selection, and PATCH /api/chat/conversations/[id] works on one conversation at a time. After a spam wave, an outage or a Monday backlog, closing or reassigning 30 chats one by one is the most tedious part of the job. First scope: shift-click/checkbox selection, x/Shift+x shortcuts, and a bar with resolve, assign, tag and snooze backed by one bulk endpoint.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Intercom.

title: Chat: Show page URL, referrer, browser, language and form answers in visitor panel
description:
Intercom shows the last page a visitor viewed when replying and offers a Recent page views sidebar app with up to 20 visits (https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/9277565-recent-page-views-app). Our widget sends no page context: app/api/chat/widget.js/route.ts never reads location.href, document.referrer, navigator.language or timezone, and components/chat/VisitorPanel.tsx only shows name, email, first seen, started, subject and CSAT, even though pre-chat answers are stored in visitor metadata.form. Knowing the visitor is on the pricing page or checkout changes the answer and saves a round of questions. First scope: send url, title, referrer, language, timezone and user agent with each visitor message, store them on the message or visitor metadata, and render them plus the form answers in the visitor panel. Also avoid using the raw external_id as the sender name in the agent notification for anonymous visitors (lib/chat-visitor-message.ts).

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with Intercom.

title: Chat: Let visitors see past conversations and unify visitors across devices
description:
Intercom's Messenger home and, since June 2026, the Customer Portal list a customer's past conversations with status and search (https://www.intercom.com/changes/en/page/1).
