Our widget only loads the latest open/pending/snoozed conversation via getOpenConversationByVisitor in lib/chat-data.ts; once resolved, the thread disappears for the visitor and the next message starts a blank conversation. Visitors are keyed by a random localStorage id, so the same person on a phone and a laptop becomes two People with split history. First scope: a 'Previous conversations' list in the widget (read only, last 10), and for verified identities (see identity gap) attach new devices to the existing visitor record by email.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Intercom.

title: Chat: Expose a public REST API and webhooks for replies, assignment and resolve
description:
Intercom's REST API covers conversations (list, search, reply, assign, close, snooze, tag, notes), contacts and tags (https://developers.intercom.com/docs/references/rest-api/api.intercom.io/conversations), and Chatwoot exposes an equivalent open API. Our public API in app/api/v1 has agents, calendar, crm and links but no chat, and emitEvent is only called in lib/chat-visitor-message.ts for conversation.created and message.received; agent replies, assignment changes and resolve emit nothing. Developers self-hosting the suite (persona 2 in PRODUCT.md) expect to pipe chats into Slack, Flow or their own tools. First scope: GET/POST /api/v1/chat/conversations and messages with API keys, plus message.sent, conversation.assigned and conversation.resolved events, documented in openapi.json.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Intercom.

title: Chat: Add custom conversation attributes and require them before resolving
description:
Intercom lets admins define conversation data attributes (e.g. topic, product area) and mark some as required before a teammate can close, which keeps reporting consistent (https://www.intercom.com/changes/en/2156-categorize-conversations-consistently-with-required-conversation-data-attributes-and-more). We only have free-form tags (lib/chat-inbox.ts) and the fixed columns of chat_conversations; reports in lib/chat-inbox.ts cannot answer 'how many billing questions this month' reliably because tags are optional and unstructured. First scope: per-widget list or text attributes edited in the conversation details panel, an optional 'required to resolve' flag enforced in PATCH, and a breakdown by attribute in reports.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Intercom.

title: Chat: Merge duplicate conversations from the same visitor into one thread
description:
Intercom offers 'Merge into' inside a conversation to combine duplicates, and users are now asking for bulk merge (https://community.intercom.com/ideas/bulk-merge-conversations-from-inbox-multi-select-14762). We have no merge: a visitor who writes again after resolve, or from the pre-chat form and a later upload, ends up with separate conversations, each with its own SLA timer and assignee (lib/chat-data.ts createChatConversation). Duplicates inflate SLA breaches and split context across teammates. First scope: a 'Merge into…' action in the conversation header limited to conversations of the same visitor, moving messages, notes and tags into the target and resolving the source with a system message.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with Intercom.

title: Chat: Push new messages in real time and add browser notifications with sound
description:
Intercom's inbox and Messenger update instantly and teammates get desktop notifications for new conversations and replies. Our inbox refreshes on a 10 s setInterval only while the tab is visible (components/chat/InboxShell.tsx) and the widget polls every 5 s (app/api/chat/widget.js/route.ts); there is no browser Notification or sound anywhere in components/chat, so an agent working in another tab only sees the in-app notification bell. Live chat lives or dies on reply speed in the first minute, and hidden-tab polling makes the team miss it. First scope: browser notifications plus an optional sound for new conversations and replies to assigned chats, and keep polling in hidden tabs at a slower rate; move to SSE later.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Intercom.

title: CRM: Find and merge duplicate companies by domain and name
description:
HubSpot merges any two records of the same object, companies and deals included, keeping activities and associations (https://knowledge.hubspot.com/records/merge-records). We only detect and merge contacts (app/api/crm/contacts/duplicates, app/api/crm/contacts/merge); app/api/crm/companies has no duplicates or merge route. Companies get duplicated easily through CSV imports, forms and Chat (company by name), and duplicate companies split deal roll-ups and the hierarchy. First scope: duplicate groups by normalized domain or exact name, a merge that moves contact/deal associations, child companies, activities, tags and custom values, reusing the contact merge pattern.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with HubSpot.

title: CRM: Let tasks repeat on a daily, weekly or monthly schedule
description:
HubSpot tasks have a 'Set to repeat' option that creates the next task in the series, also exposed through a Task series API (https://knowledge.hubspot.com/tasks/create-tasks, https://developers.hubspot.com/docs/api-reference/latest/crm/activities/task-series/guide.md). Our tasks are single crm_activities rows with due_at and done only (lib/schema/baseline.ts:159), and grepping lib/crm*.ts and components/crm finds no recurrence. Small teams use recurring tasks for account check-ins, monthly invoicing calls and renewals. First scope: a repeat rule (every N days/weeks/months) on the task form; when a task is completed, create the next one with the same owner, record links and project.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with HubSpot.

title: CRM: Support @mentions in notes and tasks with in-app and email notifications
description:
HubSpot lets users @mention teammates in activities and comments on contacts, companies and deals, and the mentioned user gets a notification if they can see the record (https://knowledge.hubspot.com/records/mention-a-user-on-a-record). Our note and task composer is a plain textarea (components/crm/Timeline.tsx:380) with no mention parsing, although lib/notifications.ts already exists and is used by lead assignment (lib/crm-assignment.ts:152). Handing a deal to a teammate today means pinging them in another tool. First scope: @ autocomplete of workspace members in the timeline composer, store mentions on the activity, notify via createNotification respecting record visibility (lib/crm-visibility.ts).

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with HubSpot.

title: CRM: Add multi-select, URL, phone, currency and user field types to custom fields
description:
HubSpot properties support single and multiple checkboxes, dropdowns, radio, number with currency formatting, date, file, HubSpot user and more (https://knowledge.hubspot.com/properties/property-field-types-in-hubspot). Our custom fields accept only text, number, date, select and boolean (lib/crm-schema.ts:276, components/crm/customPropFields.ts). Common small-team fields like 'Products of interest' (multi), 'LinkedIn URL', 'Secondary phone' or 'Account manager' (a user) end up as free text that cannot be filtered or clicked. First scope: multiselect (JSON array, 'contains any' filter), url and phone (clickable), currency-formatted number, and user (member picker, filterable like owner).

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with HubSpot.

title: CRM: Count synced emails toward deal rotting and make the threshold per stage
description:
Pipedrive lets each stage define its own 'Rotting in (days)', and sending or receiving linked emails, notes, files and done activities all reset the clock (https://support.pipedrive.com/en/article/the-rotting-feature). Our board flags a deal as rotting after a hard-coded 14 days (components/crm/DealsBoard.tsx:373), and idle time comes only from crm_activities with that deal_id or the deal's updated_at (lib/crm.ts:1531, app/[locale]/app/crm/deals/page.tsx:86). Inbound replies stored by Gmail sync never create activities (lib/crm-email-sync.ts), so a deal with an active email thread is still marked rotting, which teaches reps to ignore the badge. Fix: include the latest crm_emails sent_at for contacts associated to the deal in last activity, and add an optional rotting_days column on crm_stages editable in PipelinesEditor.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with HubSpot.

title: CRM: Require chosen properties before a deal can enter a stage
description:
HubSpot pipelines let admins mark properties as required per stage (conditional stage properties), so a deal cannot move to 'Proposal' without amount and close date; this sits in Sales Hub Professional (https://knowledge.hubspot.com/object-settings/set-up-and-customize-pipelines). Our crm_stages only store name, probability, position and won/lost flags (lib/schema/baseline.ts:119), and the move endpoint accepts any drag (app/api/crm/deals/[id]/move). Forecasts and reports are only as good as amounts and close dates, and small teams have no ops person cleaning data. Offering this for free is a cheap differentiator. First scope: required_fields JSON on crm_stages edited in PipelinesEditor, a modal on board drag or stage change that asks for missing values, enforced server-side in the move route and the v1 API.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with HubSpot.

title: CRM: Log calls and WhatsApp touches from phone links with configurable outcomes
description:
HubSpot lets admins define up to 30 custom call and meeting outcomes used when logging, in reports and in workflows, and calls can be started from a record's phone number (https://knowledge.hubspot.com/calling/create-custom-call-and-meeting-outcomes). We render phone numbers as plain tel: links (components/crm/ContactsTable.tsx:247, components/crm/RecordPreview.tsx:237) that leave no trace, and call outcome is free text (lib/crm-schema.ts:195), so it cannot be filtered or reported. HubSpot has no native WhatsApp logging (only third-party apps), and our LatAm-heavy users sell over WhatsApp daily. First scope: a workspace list of call outcomes, a 'Log this call?' prompt after clicking tel:, a WhatsApp (wa.me) action next to phones that opens the chat and logs a 'WhatsApp' touch, and outcome as a report dimension.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with HubSpot.

title: Docs: Show live presence and merge concurrent edits instead of a 409 conflict
description:
Notion lets any number of people edit the same page at once with edits appearing instantly and collaborator avatars showing where they are (https://www.notion.com/help/collaborate-with-people); Outline offers the same real-time co-editing in open source (https://www.getoutline.com/). We use optimistic concurrency: when two people save the same page, DocsEditorClient.tsx shows a conflict banner and one person must reload (losing work) or overwrite the other. In a team of 5-20 editing meeting notes together during a call, this happens every week. First scope: presence avatars and a 'someone else is editing' hint via polling or SSE, plus block-level merge on 409 (apply the other person's changed blocks when the local user did not touch them); full CRDT (Yjs) can come later.

Priority: medium. Effort: L. Compared with Notion.

title: Docs: Add filter, sort, group and board view to database blocks
description:
Notion databases offer table, board, list, calendar, timeline, gallery and chart views, with filters (AND/OR groups), multi-level sorts and group-by (https://www.notion.com/help/views-filters-and-sorts). Our DocsDatabaseBlock.tsx stores rows as string arrays with text/number/select/date columns and only toggles table or gallery, with no filter, sort, grouping, checkbox, person or URL properties. Small teams use these inline databases as lightweight trackers (content calendar, hiring list, vendor list) and without sorting or a board view they fall back to a spreadsheet. First scope: column sort and a simple per-view filter stored on the block, checkbox/person/URL column types, and a board view grouped by a select column with drag between groups.

Priority: medium. Effort: L. Compared with Notion.

title: Docs: Let teams save any page as a reusable workspace template
description:
Notion has a large template gallery plus team-made templates and database templates that prefill new pages (https://www.notion.com/templates). Our templates are four hardcoded entries in lib/docs-templates.ts (blank, meeting notes, project spec, weekly retro), and a team cannot turn its own 1:1 or incident template into a reusable starting point. Recurring documents are what small teams write most, and a shared template keeps them consistent. First scope: a 'Save as template' action in the page menu that stores title, icon and blocks in a docs_templates table per workspace, shown next to the built-ins in 'Start from a template' and in the slash menu as /template.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with Notion.

title: Docs: Select multiple blocks and move, duplicate or delete them from the keyboard
description:
Notion lets you press Esc to select the current block, extend with Shift+Arrow, then Cmd+D to duplicate, Cmd+Shift+Arrow to move and Cmd+/ to turn into another type (https://www.notion.com/help/keyboard-shortcuts). Because each block is a separate contentEditable (components/docs/DocsBlockEditor.tsx), we cannot select text across blocks, and block actions in DocsEditor.tsx (duplicate, move, turn into) are only reachable one block at a time through the grip menu. Reorganizing notes after a meeting means many mouse round trips. First scope: a block-selection mode (Esc, Shift+Up/Down, click-drag on the gutter) with Delete, Cmd+C/X/V of whole blocks, Cmd+D and Cmd+Shift+Up/Down, plus Cmd+/ opening the existing turn-into menu.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Notion.

title: Docs: Keep version history by time window and highlight what changed
description:
Notion keeps page history for 7 days on Free and 30 days on Plus, and highlights added content in blue and removed content in strikethrough (https://www.notion.com/pricing, https://www.notion.com/help/collaborate-with-people). Our lib/docs-versions.ts prunes to the last 50 snapshots per page regardless of age, with auto snapshots every 5 minutes, so one busy afternoon of edits can erase last week's versions, and VersionsPanel.tsx only previews a snapshot without a diff. When someone accidentally deletes a section, the team needs to find which version still had it. First scope: prune by age (keep all for 7 days, then one per day up to 30 days) instead of a flat count, and a block-level diff view against the current page with added/removed styling.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with Notion.

title: Docs: Add AI actions in the editor: summarize, improve, translate and draft
description:
Notion AI offers summarize, fix spelling and grammar, translate and brainstorm/draft directly on selected text or a whole page (https://www.notion.com/help/guides/using-notion-ai), and Outline answers questions about your docs (https://www.getoutline.com/). Docs has no AI at all today, while the suite already has lib/ai.ts with a per-workspace free token quota used by CRM email drafts and Notes ask. For a bilingual LATAM team, 'translate this page to English' and 'summarize these meeting notes into action items' are high-frequency and a strong differentiator for an open source suite. First scope: an AI option in the selection toolbar and slash menu (/ai) with summarize, improve writing, translate (es/en/pt) and continue writing, inserting the result as new blocks the user can accept or discard.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Notion.

title: Docs: Show backlinks ('Linked from') under the page title
description:
Notion automatically lists every page that links to the current one, visible under the title and filtered by what the viewer can access (https://www.notion.com/en-gb/help/create-links-and-backlinks). We have no backlinks anywhere in components/docs or lib/docs*.ts, and the [[ picker does not even store a link (see the related bug). Backlinks turn a pile of pages into a navigable wiki and show which docs reference an outdated policy. First scope: after fixing [[ to store page ids, compute 'Linked from' on page load by scanning workspace pages for that id (or maintain a docs_links table on save) and render it as a collapsible line under the title.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with Notion.

title: Docs: Expose a public Docs API with docs:read and docs:write scopes
description:
Notion's public API exposes pages, blocks, databases, comments and search (https://developers.notion.com/reference/block), and Notion 3.8 adds MCP access so agents can read and update the workspace (https://www.notion.com/releases); Outline also ships an open API and MCP server (https://www.getoutline.com/). Our lib/api-scopes.ts defines scopes for crm, links, cal and agents but none for docs, and there is no app/api/v1/docs, so API keys cannot create or read pages. Small teams want to push release notes or meeting summaries into Docs from scripts, Flow or Agents. First scope: /api/v1/docs/pages list/get/create/update (content as Markdown in and out using lib/docs-markdown.ts) and search, behind docs:read and docs:write, documented in the existing openapi.json.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Notion.

title: Flow: Prune old runs and steps with a retention window per workspace
description:
n8n prunes finished executions by default after 14 days or 10,000 executions, never touching waiting runs (https://docs.n8n.io/hosting/scaling/execution-data/); Zapier keeps run history for a plan-based window. Flow never deletes flow_runs, flow_steps or their stored inputs and contexts, which can reach 2 MB input and 8 MB context per run (lib/flow.ts MAX_RUN_INPUT, lib/flow-engine.ts CONTEXT_TOTAL_LIMIT), and rows are only removed when the flow itself is deleted (ON DELETE CASCADE). The UI can only show the last 100 runs anyway (listRuns clamps to 100), so older history is dead weight on Turso and a privacy liability for trigger payloads with personal data. First scope: a pruning pass in the cron tick deleting finished runs older than 30 days (env configurable for self-host), keeping waiting runs.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with Zapier / n8n.

title: Flow: Connect Google, Slack and Notion with one-click OAuth that refreshes tokens
description:
Zapier and n8n connect apps with an OAuth button and refresh tokens automatically (https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/credentials/google/oauth-single-service/). Flow credentials are pasted secrets: Google needs a service account JSON or a raw ya29 access token, and the generic oauth_token type stores only an access token with no refresh, so a pasted Google token stops working after about an hour (lib/flow-credentials-schema.ts). The repo already runs Google OAuth for Gmail and Calendar (app/api/integrations/gmail, app/api/integrations/google-calendar), so the plumbing exists. Pasting a service account is a non-starter for a founder setting up a sheet sync. First scope: OAuth connect with refresh for Google Sheets, then Slack and Notion, shown as credentials of the same types.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Zapier / n8n.

title: Flow: Add Google Sheets lookup, update and upsert rows plus a new row trigger
description:
n8n's Google Sheets node supports append or update row, update row, get rows with filters, clear and delete (https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/app-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.googlesheets/sheet-operations/), and Zapier's most used Sheets trigger is 'New or Updated Spreadsheet Row'. Our Sheets node only appends a row or reads a whole range (lib/flow-integrations.ts sheetsConfigSchema operation append|read) and there is no Sheets trigger. Sheets is the default database of small teams, so 'update the row for this deal when it is won' and 'when a row is added, create a contact' are everyday cases. First scope: lookup by column, update and upsert by key column, and a polling trigger for new rows using the schedule infrastructure.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Zapier / n8n.

title: Flow: Add AI extract and classify steps that return structured fields
description:
n8n has an Information Extractor node that returns fields from a JSON schema, a JSON example or attribute descriptions, and a Text Classifier that routes to one output per category (https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/cluster-nodes/root-nodes/n8n-nodes-langchain.information-extractor/); Zapier's AI by Zapier returns named output fields. Our ai.text node returns free text only (lib/flow-engine.ts aiNode), so using the answer in an If or a CRM field needs a JSON parse step and luck. Typical small-team flows are 'classify this inbound email or chat as sales, support or spam' and 'extract name, company and budget from this form'. First scope: an output mode on ai.text with a field list (name, type, description) using structured output, and an ai.classify node with one output handle per category.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Zapier / n8n.

title: Flow: Email the flow owner when runs fail and offer automatic replay
description:
Zapier emails owners about errors and offers autoreplay, which retries a failed step up to 5 times and holds the error email until the last attempt fails, set per account or per Zap (https://help.zapier.com/hc/en-us/articles/8496241726989). n8n uses an Error Trigger workflow. Flow has per-node retries, an optional error flow and manual rerun from a step, but nothing tells anyone a run failed unless they built an error flow themselves (no notification code in lib/flow-engine.ts finalize). Broken automations that fail silently are the main reason small teams stop trusting them. First scope: a per-flow 'notify on failure' toggle (on by default) sending one email digest per flow per hour, using the existing notifications and email modules.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with Zapier / n8n.

title: Flow: Add Wait until a date and wait for a resume call to the Delay step
description:
n8n's Wait node resumes after an interval, at a specified date and time, on a unique per-run resume webhook, or on a form submission (https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/core-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.wait/); Zapier Delay offers Delay For and Delay Until. Our Delay only waits a relative amount capped at 30 days (lib/flow-engine.ts logic.delay), so 'one day before the booking starts' or 'on the deal close date' cannot be expressed. Our apps are full of dates (bookings, deal close dates, issue due dates), which makes this especially valuable. First scope: a mode select on logic.delay with 'until' taking a templated date plus offset, and a 'resume URL' mode that reuses the hook route.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with Zapier / n8n.

title: Flow: Test a single step with pinned sample data instead of running the whole flow
description:
n8n lets you execute one node and pin its output so later test runs reuse it without calling external systems again, and edit the pinned data to test edge cases (https://docs.n8n.io/data/data-pinning/); Zapier tests each step on its own while building. Flow can test the whole flow with a manual input and rerun from a step of a past run (components/flow/FlowEditor.tsx testRun, lib/flow-engine.ts rerunFromStep), but every test fires all real side effects (Slack posts, emails, Stripe customers). First scope: a 'Test this step' button that runs one node against the last outputs (lib/flow.ts lastOutputs) or editable pinned JSON, without running downstream nodes.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Zapier / n8n.

title: Flow: Add a WhatsApp Business Cloud node to send messages and receive replies
description:
n8n ships a WhatsApp Business Cloud node and trigger, also used as an approval channel (https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/builtin/app-nodes/n8n-nodes-base.whatsapp/), and WhatsApp is among Zapier's top messaging apps. Flow has Slack, Discord and Telegram but no WhatsApp (lib/flow-integrations.ts, lib/flow-credentials-schema.ts), and the generic webhook cannot pass Meta's GET verification (see the webhook gap). Latin America is our home market (PRODUCT.md), where WhatsApp is the default channel for booking reminders, lead follow-up and support. First scope: credential (phone number id plus token), send text and template message, and a trigger for incoming messages with signature check.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Zapier / n8n.

title: Link: Make UTM fields editable and keep them in sync with the destination URL
description:
UTM params are baked into links.url at creation (applyUtm in lib/links.ts) and also stored in utm_source/medium/campaign, but linkPatchSchema has no UTM fields and EditLinkForm has no UTM inputs. If a user edits the destination and removes or changes the utm params, the stored utm_* columns and the API DTO keep reporting the old values, so the data is inconsistent. Dub treats UTM as editable link fields that set or override params in the destination (https://dub.co/docs/api-reference/endpoint/create-a-link). First scope: add utm fields to linkPatchSchema and the edit form, and re-derive the utm_* columns from the final URL on every URL change.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with Bitly / Dub.

title: Link: Add utm_term/utm_content and saved workspace UTM templates
description:
Dub's UTM builder covers all five UTM params plus ref and lets teams save workspace-level UTM templates applied from the link builder; templates are on the free plan (https://dub.co/help/article/how-to-create-utm-templates, https://dub.co/pricing/links). Our applyUtm in lib/links.ts only handles source, medium and campaign, and every link or bulk run retypes them by hand. Consistent UTM naming is the main reason small marketing teams adopt a shortener. First scope: utm_term and utm_content fields, a link_utm_templates table, and a template picker in NewLinkForm, QuickLinkModal and BulkCreateForm.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Bitly / Dub.

title: Link: Emit link.updated and link.deleted webhooks and scope click webhooks
description:
Dub emits link.created, link.updated, link.deleted and link.clicked, and since July 2026 click webhooks can target all links, selected folders or selected links (https://dub.co/docs/concepts/webhooks/event-types, https://dub.co/changelog/improve-link-clicked-webhook). Our WEBHOOK_EVENTS in lib/webhooks-events.ts has only link.created and link.clicked; applyLinkPatch, the DELETE routes and bulkLinkAction emit nothing. Anyone syncing links to a sheet, CRM or Flow cannot see edits or deletions, and click webhooks fire for every link in the workspace. First scope: emit link.updated and link.deleted (single and bulk) and add an optional tag filter on link.clicked subscriptions.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with Bitly / Dub.

title: Link: Extend v1 API create with UTM, expiry, password, OG, targeting and externalId
description:
Dub's create link endpoint accepts utm_*, expiresAt, expiredUrl, password, preview fields, geo/ios/android, A/B variants, tagNames, folderId and an externalId for upserts (https://dub.co/docs/api-reference/endpoint/create-a-link). Our POST /api/v1/links createSchema only takes url, domain, slug, title and tags, even though createLink supports UTM, expiry, password, max clicks and OG; it even maps an invalid_date error it can never produce. There are also no v1 endpoints for tags, domains or bulk create. First scope: pass every CreateLinkInput field through v1, add externalId with lookup and upsert, and expose GET /api/v1/links/domains and bulk create.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with Bitly / Dub.

title: Link: Publish a shareable read-only analytics page for a link or tag
description:
Dub lets you publish a public analytics dashboard for a link or folder, optionally password protected, so clients and stakeholders see results without an invite (https://dub.co/help/article/share-analytics). Our analytics live only behind the session in app/[locale]/app/links/[id] and app/api/links/[id]/analytics; there is no public token. Agencies and small teams reporting to a client today export CSVs or screenshots. First scope: a share toggle that mints a token URL rendering the existing per-link chart and breakdowns read-only, with optional password reuse from the gate.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Bitly / Dub.

title: Link: Record who created each link and filter the list by creator
description:
Dub workspaces show the creator on each link card and support role-based access across team members (https://dub.co/data-model, https://dub.co/help/article/folders-rbac). Our links table only stores user_id, which is the workspace owner (lib/session.ts resolves the effective user to the owner), so in a shared workspace nobody can tell who made a link or find their own. This is the first thing a 5 to 20 person team asks for after inviting colleagues. First scope: created_by column filled from the acting user, avatar in LinksTable, and a 'created by' filter in FilterBar and the API.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with Bitly / Dub.

title: Notes: Keep version history so a note can be previewed and restored
description:
Evernote's Note history lets you preview past versions by date, restore one, or export it (https://help.evernote.com/hc/articles/208313858). Our notes table stores only the current content and there is no history table or UI (lib/notes.ts, lib/schema/migrations.ts 018_notes_core), while Docs already has a versions module (lib/docs-versions.ts) that could be reused. With autosave on every keystroke pause, an accidental select-all delete is unrecoverable. First scope: snapshot content at most every 10 minutes of editing and before restore, keep the last 30 per note, and add a History panel with preview and restore.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Evernote.

title: Notes: Turn a note or selected checklist items into Track issues with a backlink
description:
Evernote's 2026 releases push notes toward action: tasks inside notes, AI Assistant that creates events, and calendar suggestions after meeting recordings (https://releasebot.io/updates/evernote, https://help.evernote.com/hc/articles/1500003792141). Our todos inside a note are inert checkboxes and Notes has no link to Track even though lib/track-data.ts exposes createIssue. For small teams, meeting notes are where work gets discovered, and moving it to Track by hand is where it gets lost. First scope: a 'Create issue in Track' action on a note and on selected todo blocks, choosing the team, prefilling title and description, and inserting a link to the new issue back into the note.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Evernote.

title: Notes: Share a note or notebook with workspace teammates with view or edit access
description:
Evernote lets you share a notebook by email with a permission level and groups shared content in Spaces with view or edit access (https://help.evernote.com/hc/en-us/articles/209005657). Our only sharing mode is a public read-only link, and the privacy model explicitly prevents teammates in the same workspace from seeing each other's notes (lib/notes.ts header comment, setNoteShared). For a suite sold to teams of 2 to 50, a private note that cannot be handed to a colleague for editing forces people to copy it into Docs. First scope: share a single note with specific workspace members as viewer or editor, a 'Shared with me' view, and a 'Promote to Docs page' action for notes that become team knowledge.

Priority: medium. Effort: L. Compared with Evernote.

title: Notes: Clip full articles and bookmarks, not only the selected text
description:
Evernote's Web Clipper offers Article, Simplified article, Full page, Bookmark and Screenshot modes (https://help.evernote.com/hc/en-us/articles/209125827). Our bookmarklet only sends URL, title and the current selection, truncated to 4000 characters in a query string, and the server stores the selection as quote blocks (lib/notes-types.ts clipBookmarklet and clipBlocks). With nothing selected the note is just a link, so 'save this article to read later' does not work. First scope: when no selection is made, fetch the URL server-side, extract the main article with a readability-style pass into sanitized blocks, and store the page description and favicon for bookmark clips; send the selection via POST message instead of the URL to lift the 4000 character cap.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Evernote.

title: Notes: Add a personal inbound email address that turns forwarded email into notes
description:
Evernote gives every user a private address; forwarded emails become notes, and the subject line accepts @notebook and #tag shortcuts, up to 200 emails per day (https://help.evernote.com/hc/articles/209005347). We have no inbound capture besides the bookmarklet (app/api/notes has no email route), although the suite already sends and receives email through Resend and CRM email sync. Forwarding receipts, confirmations and threads is one of the fastest capture habits and works from any phone mail client. First scope: a per-person secret address shown in Notes settings, an inbound webhook that creates a note with subject as title and body as blocks, and @notebook and #tag parsing in the subject.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Evernote.

title: Notes: Support search operators like tag:, notebook:, intitle:, created: and todo:
description:
Evernote supports advanced search syntax such as intitle:coffee, tag:travel, created:20240101 and relative dates like created:day-7, combinable in one query (https://help.evernote.com/hc/articles/208313828). Our searchTerms strips everything except letters and digits (lib/notes-types.ts), so 'tag:clip' becomes two plain words, and tags are not indexed in notes_fts at all. Power users with hundreds of notes rely on these filters to find things fast. First scope: parse tag:, notebook:, intitle:, created:/updated: with day-N and week-N, and todo:true/false into SQL filters before running the FTS match, and index tags in FTS.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with Evernote.

title: Notes: Link notes to each other with [[ ]] and show backlinks
description:
Evernote supports note links that jump between notes and a backlinks panel listing every note that links to the current one (https://help.evernote.com/hc/articles/208313588, https://evernote.com/blog/introducing-backlinks/); Obsidian and Bear make this the core of their model. The Docs editor has a [[ page mention menu but it is explicitly disabled when embedded in Notes (components/docs/DocsEditor.tsx, mentionMatch is null when embedded). Linking turns isolated notes into a personal knowledge base and is expected by anyone migrating from Obsidian or Bear. First scope: enable [[ in Notes against the person's own notes, store links in a note_links table on save, and show a Backlinks section under the note.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Evernote.

title: Notes: Import Evernote ENEX and Markdown files, and export notes as Markdown
description:
Evernote exports notebooks as ENEX and Obsidian's official Importer converts ENEX to Markdown, including tags and stacks (https://obsidian.md/help/import/evernote); Evernote's free plan is capped at 50 notes and 1 notebook (https://help.evernote.com/hc/en-us/articles/23565231682323), which pushes users to switch. We have no import or export path for Notes (no route under app/api/notes), while the suite already has importers for CRM and Bitly and a Docs Markdown converter (lib/docs-markdown.ts). A one-click Evernote import is the single strongest acquisition hook against a paywalled incumbent, and Markdown export fits our open source promise of no lock-in. First scope: upload an .enex file, map notebooks, tags, created/updated dates and basic formatting to blocks; plus a 'Download as Markdown' action per note and a zip for all notes.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Evernote.

title: Robots: Add continue-on-error per step and per loop item with a warnings status
description:
Axiom.ai offers Continue on error, a Try/Catch step, and loops that log a warning for a failing row instead of stopping, plus 'succeeded with warnings' notifications (https://axiom.ai/docs/no-code-tool/reference/settings/error-handling/continue-on-error/, https://axiom.ai/blog/getting-to-know-the-trycatch-step/). In our runList any failed step throws and aborts the whole run, including one bad item inside a loop_over of 50 URLs (lib/robots-interpreter.ts), and RobotRunStatus only has success and failed. Losing 49 good results because of one broken page makes loop robots unusable. First scope: onError: 'fail' | 'continue' on leaf steps and loop_over, collect per-item errors into vars.errors, and a new 'partial' run status shown in RunsPanel and emitted in robot.run.finished.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with UiPath (StudioX, Autopilot, Orchestrator, Healing Agent), Browse AI, Axiom.ai, Bardeen, Browserbase/Stagehand, Skyvern.

title: Robots: Detect changes between runs and emit a robot.output.changed event with a diff
description:
Browse AI monitors re-run a robot on a schedule and alert by email or webhook when captured text, lists or a screenshot change beyond a 1/5/10% threshold (https://www.browse.ai/monitoring, https://intercom.help/browse-ai-089fe61c5dc3/en/articles/10535487-how-can-i-setup-monitoring-for-changes). Our price-check template runs daily but nothing compares the output to the previous run; the only events are finished and failed (lib/robots.ts, lib/flow-schema.ts). Competitor price, job board and stock monitoring is the most common small team use case and it needs 'tell me only when it changed'. First scope: per-robot 'watch variables' list, compare against the last successful run output, store a diff (added/removed rows, changed values) on the run, and emit robot.output.changed for Flow and webhooks.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with UiPath (StudioX, Autopilot, Orchestrator, Healing Agent), Browse AI, Axiom.ai, Bardeen, Browserbase/Stagehand, Skyvern.

title: Robots: Upsert extracted rows into CRM contacts and companies with mapping and dedupe
description:
Bardeen positions scraping straight into GTM tools (scrape, enrich, export to CRM) with credits per scraped row (https://www.bardeen.ai/pricing), and Axiom.ai writes scrape results directly to Google Sheets (https://axiom.ai/guides/scrape-links-from-a-website/). Today a robot table reaches our CRM only by building a Flow with app.crm_contact per row, and the only robot template in Flow is robotToSheets (lib/flow-schema.ts). Robot output landing as deduplicated CRM records is something no standalone scraper can do natively and exploits our suite. First scope: a robot 'Destinations' panel that maps one table variable to CRM contacts or companies (column to field, dedupe by email or domain, source tag = robot name), applied after each successful run, with counts created/updated in the run view.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with UiPath (StudioX, Autopilot, Orchestrator, Healing Agent), Browse AI, Axiom.ai, Bardeen, Browserbase/Stagehand, Skyvern.

title: Robots: Add a TOTP secret to credentials so robots can log in behind 2FA
description:
Skyvern stores an authenticator key on a password credential and generates a fresh TOTP code at login, using the next code if fewer than 20 seconds remain (https://www.skyvern.com/docs/credentials/totp/, https://skyvern.com/docs/developers/features/authentication-and-2fa). Our credential types are api_key, basic, oauth_token and app tokens with no TOTP field (lib/flow-credentials-schema.ts), and the recorder deliberately masks one-time-code fields (lib/robots-recorder.ts), so a 2FA login can only work while a persisted session survives. Most admin portals small teams automate (banks, tax sites, supplier portals) require 2FA. First scope: optional totpSecret (secret) on the basic type and a {{credentials.NAME.totp}} template value computed at use time inside the interpreter, redacted like other secrets.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with UiPath (StudioX, Autopilot, Orchestrator, Healing Agent), Browse AI, Axiom.ai, Bardeen, Browserbase/Stagehand, Skyvern.

title: Robots: Replace the robot id text box in the Flow node with a picker that loads inputs
description:
UiPath Orchestrator and Axiom.ai let you pick the automation to trigger and show its parameters (https://docs.uipath.com/orchestrator/docs/alerts, https://www.axiom.ai/docs/no-code-tool/how-it-works/loop). Our app.robot_run node defines robotId as a plain text field with placeholder 'robot id' and inputs as free key/value pairs (lib/flow-schema.ts), and nothing in components/flow resolves robots, while sub-flows get a flowRef picker. Users must copy a UUID from the URL and guess input names, so 'trigger a robot from Flow' is technically present but hard to use. First scope: a robotRef field kind that lists workspace robots and prefills the inputs kv with the robot's declared input names and required flags, plus outputs autocompletion for {{steps.x.output.var}}.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with UiPath (StudioX, Autopilot, Orchestrator, Healing Agent), Browse AI, Axiom.ai, Bardeen, Browserbase/Stagehand, Skyvern.

title: Robots: Add natural-language act and extract steps backed by the AI gateway with caching
description:
Stagehand exposes act(), extract() with a schema and observe(), caches resolved actions keyed by instruction and page content, and self-heals when a cached selector stops resolving (https://docs.stagehand.dev/v4/basics/act, https://docs.stagehand.dev/v4/best-practices/caching); UiPath Autopilot generates StudioX workflows from a plain-language description (https://docs.uipath.com/studiox/standalone/2024.10/release-notes/2024-10-1). Our steps all require CSS selectors or exact visible text and there is no AI step type (lib/robots-schema.ts STEP_TYPES). AI steps lower the skill bar for non-technical members and fix brittle selectors. First scope: an 'ai_extract' step (instruction plus field list, returns rows) and an 'ai_click' step that resolves an element from an accessibility snapshot once, caches the chosen selector on the robot, and re-resolves only on failure.

Priority: medium. Effort: L. Compared with UiPath (StudioX, Autopilot, Orchestrator, Healing Agent), Browse AI, Axiom.ai, Bardeen, Browserbase/Stagehand, Skyvern.

title: Robots: Expose a public API to run robots and bulk-run one robot over many inputs
description:
Browse AI has a REST API with tasks history and POST /v2/robots/{robotId}/bulk-runs that queues up to 1,000 input sets per call (https://www.browse.ai/monitoring), and Axiom.ai has a developer API to trigger bots (https://axiom.ai/docs/developer-hub/api/reference/errorcodes/). Our run endpoint requires an admin session cookie (app/api/robots/[id]/run/route.ts, canEditRobots in lib/robots-http.ts) and app/api/v1 has agents, calendar, crm and links but no robots. Teams want to run a robot from their own scripts, Zapier or a spreadsheet of 200 URLs. First scope: /api/v1/robots/{id}/runs (POST with inputs, GET list) and /api/v1/runs/{id} using existing API keys, plus a bulk endpoint that enqueues runs once the queue from the busy fix exists; document in openapi.json.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with UiPath (StudioX, Autopilot, Orchestrator, Healing Agent), Browse AI, Axiom.ai, Bardeen, Browserbase/Stagehand, Skyvern.

title: Track: Add Cmd+K command menu and single-key shortcuts for issue properties
description:
Linear is driven by a command menu and single-key actions: S status, A assign, P priority, L labels, G then I for inbox, H snooze, and ? opens a searchable shortcut help (https://linear.app/docs/inbox, https://linear.app/changelog/2021-03-25-keyboard-shortcuts-help). Track only handles C, J/K and Enter (components/track/TrackShortcuts.tsx). Without property shortcuts, triaging a list means opening every popover with the mouse. First scope: on the focused row or open issue, S/A/P/L open the existing inline editors from components/track/InlineEditors.tsx, plus Cmd+K with go-to and change-property commands and a ? help dialog.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Linear.

title: Track: Add issue templates per project with preset properties and description
description:
Linear templates preset properties and description, can be form templates with required fields, and a team can set a default template for new issues and for integrations (https://linear.app/docs/issue-templates). Track has no template concept: QuickIssueModal (components/track/QuickIssueModal.tsx) always starts blank and createIssue in lib/track-data.ts takes no template. Bug reports from teammates arrive without repro steps or environment. First scope: per-project templates (title prefix, description, labels, priority, status), a picker in the new-issue modal, and an optional default template, also applied to chat and flow sources.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Linear.

title: Track: Support recurring issues on a daily, weekly, monthly or yearly schedule
description:
Linear lets you make an issue recurring (daily, weekly, monthly, yearly); the next instance is created when the previous one hits its due date, and recurring issues are managed in team settings (https://linear.app/changelog/2024-12-05-recurring-issues, https://linear.app/docs/ops-and-marketing). In Track the only route is building a Flow with a schedule trigger and the app.track_issue action (lib/flow-schema.ts), which is far from the issue itself. Ops chores like invoicing, backups or monthly reports are a core small-team use. First scope: a Make recurring option on an issue with a frequency, stored rule, and a cron that clones title, description, labels and assignee with the next due date.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Linear.

title: Track: Add snooze and remind-me to the inbox and issues
description:
In Linear, H snoozes an inbox item until a preset or typed time and new activity cancels the snooze; Remind me sends an inbox notification at a chosen time without hiding the issue (https://linear.app/docs/snooze). Track's inbox (components/track/InboxClient.tsx) only supports read and mark-all-read, with no snooze or reminder fields. Small teams use reminders to follow up on blocked work instead of keeping a separate to-do list. First scope: snoozed_until on notifications with presets (later today, tomorrow, next week), and a Remind me action on the issue that schedules a notification via the existing cron.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with Linear.

title: Track: Search issue descriptions and comments, and escape LIKE wildcards
description:
Linear search covers issue content and comments across the workspace (Cmd/Ctrl+F quick search, https://linear.app/docs/inbox). Track search only matches title or identifier (lib/track-data.ts listIssues and listAllIssues use title LIKE ? OR identifier LIKE ?), so you cannot find an issue by an error message pasted in its description. The query is also interpolated as %q% without escaping, so a search for 100% or snake_case matches unexpected rows. First scope: include description text and comment bodies in the search (SQLite FTS5 table or LIKE with ESCAPE), and escape % and _ in user input.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with Linear.

title: Track: Add group by and more sort options to list and board views
description:
Linear display options let you group lists and boards by status, assignee, priority, cycle, label or project and order by priority, due date, updated or manual (https://linear.app/docs/display-options). Track's board only groups by status (components/track/IssuesBoard.tsx), the project list has no grouping, and the saved view sort enum is limited to newest, oldest, priority and identifier (lib/track-schema.ts issueViewCreateSchema). A lead reviewing workload per person or sorting by deadline cannot do it in the project view. First scope: groupBy (status, assignee, priority, cycle, label) for list and board, sort by due date and last updated, both persisted in saved views.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Linear.

title: Track: Share saved views with the team and allow workspace-level views
description:
Linear views can be personal or shared with a team or the workspace, and filtered views can be shared by URL or shortcut (https://linear.app/changelog, Jul 2, 2026 entry). Track saved views are filtered by user_id in listIssueViews (lib/track-data.ts), so each teammate has to rebuild the same Bugs this week view, and views only exist inside one project. First scope: a visibility flag (personal or team) on track_issue_views, shared views listed for all project members, and saved views on the cross-project Issues page.

Priority: medium. Effort: S. Compared with Linear.

title: Track: Add milestones with target dates and progress inside a project
description:
Linear projects can be split into milestones with optional target dates, each showing completion percentage from its issues in the overview and timeline (https://linear.app/docs/project-milestones), and projects carry health updates (on track, at risk, off track) (https://linear.app/docs/initiative-and-project-updates). Track has no layer between a project and its issues: track_projects has no target date or lead and there is no milestone table (lib/schema/baseline.ts). Small teams shipping a launch need to see whether phase 1 is done before the deadline. First scope: track_milestones (name, target date, position), a milestone property on issues, progress per milestone on the project page and in the Gantt view.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Linear.

title: Agents: Support secret headers on http_request so agents can call authenticated APIs
description:
http_request only sends a fixed user-agent and content-type to allowlisted domains (lib/agent-tools.ts) and toolsConfigSchema has no place for credentials (lib/agents-config.ts), so it can only reach public endpoints. Fin connects to internal systems via Data Connectors or MCP with control over what data is exposed (https://production.fin.ai/procedures), and Zapier Agents act across thousands of authenticated apps. First scope: per-domain encrypted headers (for example Authorization) stored server-side and never shown to the model, optional named endpoints with a description and JSON schema so the model picks an endpoint rather than composing raw URLs.

Priority: low. Effort: S. Compared with Intercom Fin, Zapier Agents, Lindy (plus OpenAI AgentKit as reference for evals/versioning).

title: Agents: Show API and Flow usage in the agent list channels and 7-day counts
description:
listAgents in lib/agents.ts only pushes 'chat' and 'public' into channels even though AgentListItem allows 'api', so agents used through /api/v1/agents or the Flow agent node (lib/flow-engine.ts agentNode, which also runs as channel 'api') look unused in the list. Fin's reporting breaks volume down by channel (https://fin.ai/pricing). Owners cleaning up agents could delete one that a Flow depends on. First scope: add 'api' when the agent has any api-channel conversation in the last 30 days and list referencing flows on the agent page, warning before delete.

Priority: low. Effort: S. Compared with Intercom Fin, Zapier Agents, Lindy (plus OpenAI AgentKit as reference for evals/versioning).

title: Board: Present frames as slides and export frames to PDF
description:
Miro reads frame order from the board, shows them in a sidebar outline and presents them as slides, and exports high-resolution PDF/JPG on Starter (https://miro.com/pricing/, https://miro.com/blog/what-we-launched-october-2022/). Excalidraw gives us frames, but components/board/ExcalidrawCanvas.tsx only enables the stock export dialog (single PNG/SVG of the canvas or selection) and there is no presentation mode or frame list. Teams reuse board content in reviews and client calls, which today means screenshots. First scope: a frames panel listing frames in order with click-to-zoom, a fullscreen 'Present' mode stepping through frames with arrow keys, and 'Export frames as PDF' using exportToBlob per frame.

Priority: low. Effort: M. Compared with Miro.

title: Board: Fix editor rename that skips saves, shows no errors and keeps stale updated_at
description:
saveName in components/board/BoardEditor.tsx compares against the initial board.name prop, so renaming A to B and back to A in the same session never saves the second change, and the PATCH result is ignored so failures leave the UI showing a name the server does not have. renameBoard in lib/boards.ts also does not touch updated_at, so the list ordering and 'updated' meta in components/board/BoardList.tsx ignore renames. Miro renames are immediate and reflected in board lists. First scope: track the last saved name in a ref, surface errors with the existing status text, and bump updated_at on rename.

Priority: low. Effort: S. Compared with Miro.

title: Cal: Support group events with seats so several invitees can book one slot
description:
Calendly Group event types let one host meet multiple invitees per slot (webinars, classes, tours), and Cal.com offers seats with capacity (https://calendly.com/help/event-types-overview, https://cal.com/blog/discover-cal-com-s-advanced-settings). Our booking INSERT in lib/calendar.ts rejects any overlap for the host and there is a unique index on host and start, so a slot holds exactly one booking. Trainers, onboarding sessions and office hours need this weekly. First scope: seats per event type, count bookings per slot instead of rejecting overlap, show remaining seats on the booking page, and one shared Google event with attendees added.

Priority: low. Effort: L. Compared with Calendly.

title: Cal: Distribute round-robin bookings fairly and expose a no-show webhook event
description:
Calendly round robin can optimize for availability or for equal distribution, and its API emits invitee_no_show.created webhooks (https://calendly.com/help/how-to-use-buffers mentions distribution effects; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/calendlyv2). In lib/calendar.ts createBooking increments rr_cursor by one whatever host pickFreeHost chose, so when the cursor host is busy the next host gets two bookings in a row and the skipped one loses its turn. Separately, the v1 no-show endpoint (app/api/v1/calendar/bookings/[id]/no-show/route.ts) never calls emitEvent, so webhooks and Flow cannot react to no-shows. First scope: set the cursor to the index after the host actually picked (or pick the least recently booked free host), and emit booking.no_show from both the admin and v1 paths.

Priority: low. Effort: S. Compared with Calendly.

title: Chat: Add AI compose tools for agents: summarize to note, rephrase, translate
description:
Intercom's inbox AI lets teammates expand shorthand, change tone, fix grammar and translate a reply (Cmd+J), and summarize a conversation into an editable internal note (https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/6955446-fin-ai-for-help-desk). We already call the AI Gateway for the visitor-facing bot in lib/chat-bot-ai.ts, but the agent composer in components/chat/ConversationClient.tsx has no AI actions. This is agent assist, separate from the backlog items for a docs-answering bot and action-taking agents. First scope: a composer menu with 'Rephrase', 'Translate to visitor language' and 'Summarize to note', billed through the existing usage metering and hidden when AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY is absent.

Priority: low. Effort: M. Compared with Intercom.

title: Chat: Allow editing and deleting internal notes and agent messages
description:
Intercom made internal notes editable by their author in March 2026, behind a 'Can edit notes' permission (https://www.intercom.com/changes/en/page/1). Our messages route app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/messages/route.ts only implements GET and POST, so a note with a wrong @mention, a typo in a reply or a pasted secret stays forever. First scope: PATCH and DELETE for the author's own notes (and agent replies not yet read by the visitor), with an 'edited' marker, and re-evaluate mentions on edit.

Priority: low. Effort: S. Compared with Intercom.

title: Chat: Export conversation transcripts and email a transcript to the visitor
description:
Intercom added bulk export of conversations as PDF or plain text from the actions menu in June 2026 (https://www.intercom.com/changes/en/page/1), and Crisp and Chatwoot let agents send the transcript to the customer by email. We export only aggregate report rows as CSV (chatReportToCsv in lib/chat-inbox.ts); a single thread can only be copied by hand or logged to the CRM. Teams need transcripts for refunds, disputes and handing context to someone outside the tool. First scope: 'Download transcript' (text) in the conversation menu, an 'Email transcript' action to the visitor's email, and a CSV of messages in the reports export.

Priority: low. Effort: S. Compared with Intercom.

title: CRM: Add an AI summary card on contact, company and deal pages
description:
HubSpot's Breeze record summary card generates on record load from activities, notes and ownership, can be refreshed, and is also a workflow action (https://knowledge.hubspot.com/records/summarize-records). Our only AI touch in the CRM is 'Draft with AI' for emails (components/crm/Timeline.tsx:432, app/api/crm/emails/draft); there is no record summary. Before a call, a founder wants 'where is this deal and what was promised' without scrolling a long timeline. First scope: when AI is enabled, a cached summary card above the timeline built from the last N activities, emails and stage changes, with a refresh button and a 'next step' suggestion; no automatic writes.

Priority: low. Effort: M. Compared with HubSpot.

title: CRM: Attach files to notes and records, not only to tasks
description:
HubSpot has an Attachments card on every record and an attach button in the note and activity editor (https://knowledge.hubspot.com/records/add-and-remove-attachments-from-records). We only store files for tasks (crm_task_files, components/crm/TaskFiles.tsx); notes are a plain textarea with no attachments (components/crm/Timeline.tsx:380), and contacts, companies and deals have no files panel. Signed contracts, briefs and screenshots end up in Drive with no link to the deal. First scope: generalize crm_task_files into activity and record attachments, an attach icon in the note composer, and an Attachments side panel on record pages that respects record visibility.

Priority: low. Effort: M. Compared with HubSpot.

title: CRM: Show company logos and prefill basic company data from the domain
description:
Attio enriches company records from the domain on its Free plan, logo included, as soon as a record is created (https://attio.com/help/reference/managing-your-data/enriched-data), while HubSpot moved enrichment to paid Breeze Intelligence and turned it off by default (https://knowledge.hubspot.com/records/get-started-with-data-enrichment). We store name, domain, industry and employees typed by hand (lib/schema/baseline.ts:92) and show no logo anywhere. Logos make lists and the board scannable, and free enrichment is a visible differentiator against HubSpot. First scope: logo from the domain favicon (cached, no third-party tracking) on company rows, cards and headers, plus an optional fetch of the site's title and meta description into empty fields.

Priority: low. Effort: S. Compared with HubSpot.

title: Docs: Add web bookmarks, video embeds and two-column layout
description:
Notion embeds YouTube, Loom, Figma and other links, renders web bookmarks as preview cards, and lets you drag blocks side by side into resizable columns (https://www.notion.com/help/images-files-and-media, https://www.notion.com/help/columns-headings-and-dividers). Our block schema (lib/docs-schema.ts) has no embed, bookmark or column type, and the sanitizer drops IFRAME/EMBED (lib/docs-richtext.ts), so a pasted Loom link stays a plain link. Async teams share Loom walkthroughs and Figma files inside specs constantly. First scope: when a lone URL is pasted, offer 'Embed' for an allowlist of providers (YouTube, Vimeo, Loom, Figma, Google Docs) and 'Bookmark' for anything else (fetch title, description and favicon server side); columns can follow as a second step.

Priority: low. Effort: M. Compared with Notion.

title: Link: Group links into folders with view or edit access per folder
description:
Dub Pro includes folders, and Business adds per-folder access (can edit, can view, no access) with members added to private folders (https://dub.co/help/article/link-folders, https://dub.co/help/article/folders-rbac). Bitly Campaigns groups links by channel for side by side comparison (https://support.bitly.com/hc/en-us/articles/115001195167). We only have up to 5 free-text tags per link (lib/links.ts), no folder entity and no permission below workspace level. First scope: a link_folders table, folder picker in create/edit, folder filter in the list and analytics; access levels can follow later.

Priority: low. Effort: M. Compared with Bitly / Dub.

title: Link: Capture city, region and full referrer URL on each click
description:
Dub exposes regions, cities and referer_urls as analytics dimensions, and Bitly keeps city-level data as a premium upsell (https://dub.co/docs/api-reference/endpoint/retrieve-analytics, https://bitly.com/pages/pricing). contextFromHeaders in lib/track.ts stores only the referrer hostname and country, although Vercel already sends x-vercel-ip-city and x-vercel-ip-country-region headers on the same request. Local businesses and event promoters care more about the city than the country. First scope: add city, region and referrer_url columns to clicks, fill them from the platform headers, and show them in breakdowns and CSV exports.

Priority: low. Effort: S. Compared with Bitly / Dub.

title: Link: Allow domain choice and per-row slug and title in bulk create
description:
Bitly Growth offers bulk link and QR creation from an upload, and Dub's bulk endpoints accept the full link payload per row, including domain and key (https://bitly.com/pages/pricing, https://dub.co/docs/api-reference/endpoint/create-a-link). Our createLinksBulk in lib/links.ts only takes a list of URLs plus one tag and UTM set, always on the default domain, with random slugs; BulkCreateForm has no domain selector. Teams with a branded domain have to create campaign links one by one to keep them on brand. First scope: a domain select in BulkCreateForm and CSV paste with url,slug,title columns reusing the bitly-import parser.

Priority: low. Effort: S. Compared with Bitly / Dub.

title: Link: Add internal comments and a duplicate action to links
description:
Dub lets teams add comments to a link, shown as a bubble on the link card, and stores them as a comments field in the API (https://dub.co/help/article/link-comments); Short.io exposes duplicate link actions in its API (https://help.short.io/en/articles/9790533-how-to-delete-links). Our links have only a title (lib/links.ts schema) and LinksTable row actions are copy, QR, edit, archive and delete with no duplicate. Notes like 'used in the October print flyer' and cloning a link to vary the UTM are routine for marketers. First scope: a comments text column editable in EditLinkForm with an icon in the row, and a Duplicate row action that opens the create form prefilled.

Priority: low. Effort: S. Compared with Bitly / Dub.

title: Notes: Make Notes an installable PWA with offline reading and queued edits
description:
Evernote, Apple Notes, Keep, Bear and Obsidian all work offline on mobile, and Evernote documents which search operators still work offline (https://help.evernote.com/hc/articles/208313828). Our app has no web manifest or service worker (no app/manifest, nothing in public/), every list and note load is a network fetch (components/notes/NotesApp.tsx refreshList, openNote), and a failed save only shows an error status. On a phone with weak signal, capture fails exactly when it is needed. First scope: a web manifest so Notes can be added to the home screen, caching of recently opened notes in IndexedDB, and an offline save queue that replays PATCHes when back online.

Priority: low. Effort: L. Compared with Evernote.

title: Notes: Show column headers for database blocks on shared and trashed notes
description:
Evernote's shared and published notes render tables faithfully, and its September 2026 release added header row toggles for tables (https://releasebot.io/updates/evernote). Our read-only renderer treats database blocks like plain tables and prints only rows, ignoring the columns array that holds the column names (components/notes/NoteBlocksView.tsx, DocsBlock.columns in lib/docs-types.ts). Anyone opening a shared link to a note with a database block sees an unlabeled grid. First scope: render a thead from block.columns for database blocks in NoteBlocksView.

Priority: low. Effort: S. Compared with Evernote.

title: Robots: Let Agents use robots as tools to browse and act on websites
description:
Browserbase and Stagehand are built so AI agents can drive a real browser (https://docs.stagehand.dev/), and Skyvern runs LLM-driven workflows with login blocks (https://skyvern.com/docs/developers/features/authentication-and-2fa). Our Agents product has no browser or robot tool: nothing under lib/agent* or app/api/agents references robots, and startRobotRun is called only from the run route and the Flow engine. Exposing existing robots (with their typed inputs) as agent tools turns Robots into the 'hands' of the suite without building a general browser agent. First scope: agent setting to attach up to 5 robots; each becomes a tool whose JSON schema is generated from robotInputSchema, runs with trigger 'agent', and returns output vars plus screenshot URLs.

Priority: low. Effort: M. Compared with UiPath (StudioX, Autopilot, Orchestrator, Healing Agent), Browse AI, Axiom.ai, Bardeen, Browserbase/Stagehand, Skyvern.

title: Robots: Export run tables to CSV and prune old runs with a retention policy
description:
Browse AI lets users download captured lists and keeps task data for a plan-based retention window (https://www.saaspricepulse.com/tools/browse-ai), and Browserbase states 7-day data retention on its free plan (https://docs.browserbase.com/guides/plans-and-pricing). Our RunsPanel can show output as a table but only offers copying the JSON (components/robots/RunsPanel.tsx), and nothing ever deletes robot_runs rows, which store up to 200 KB of output and 600 log entries each, so a 15-minute schedule grows the table without bound (lib/robots.ts, lib/schema/migrations.ts). First scope: a 'Download CSV' button per table variable, and a cron cleanup that keeps the last 200 runs or 90 days per robot (configurable via env) while keeping the latest success.

Priority: low. Effort: S. Compared with UiPath (StudioX, Autopilot, Orchestrator, Healing Agent), Browse AI, Axiom.ai, Bardeen, Browserbase/Stagehand, Skyvern.

title: Track: Create issues from email with a per-project intake address
description:
Linear gives each team a unique intake email; new emails become issues in triage with sender and attachments, and replies do not create new issues (https://linear.app/integrations/create-issues-via-email, https://linear.app/docs/customer-requests). Track already has a triage queue for non-app sources (lib/track-bulk.ts, source column) but no email entry point. Customers and non-users report bugs by email, so this turns Track into a lightweight help desk for small teams. First scope: a per-project address using the existing inbound email handling, issues created with source email and triage on, sender stored on the issue, attachments copied.

Priority: low. Effort: M. Compared with Linear.

title: Track: Log activity and emit events when completing a cycle moves issues
description:
completeCycle in lib/track-data.ts moves unfinished issues with a raw UPDATE on track_issues, so no cycle_change activity is written, no issue.updated Flow event fires, and assignees get no notice, unlike updateIssue and bulk edit, which keep activity and notifications (lib/track-bulk.ts). Linear keeps the issue history and the cycle snapshot when rolling over (https://linear.app/docs/use-cycles). The issue timeline then shows a cycle that silently changed. First scope: collect moved issue ids in the transaction, then write cycle_change activities and emit issue.updated for each after commit.

Priority: low. Effort: S. Compared with Linear.

title: Agents: Upload PDF, DOCX, TXT and CSV files as knowledge
description: Chatbase trains on PDF, TXT, DOC and DOCX up to 20 MB each (https://www.chatbase.co/docs/user-guides/chatbot/data-sources.md) and Voiceflow imports PDF, DOCX and CSV/XLSX tables where each row becomes a chunk (https://www.voiceflow.com/docs/documentation/build/importing-data-sources.md). Our Knowledge tab only takes Docs pages, up to 20 URLs and Chat saved replies (knowledgeConfigSchema in lib/agents-config.ts); there is no file input (verified in the browser). Price lists and manuals usually live in PDFs. First scope: upload files to an agent (reuse the Docs upload storage), extract text server side, chunk and index them next to URLs for search_knowledge, show size, status and re-upload, with a per-workspace size cap.

title: Agents: Crawl a whole site or sitemap with include and exclude patterns
description: Chatbase crawls a website or sitemap and auto-resyncs weekly (https://www.chatbase.co/docs/user-guides/chatbot/data-sources.md); Voiceflow manages sitemaps with include/exclude patterns and a refresh schedule (https://www.voiceflow.com/docs/documentation/build/importing-data-sources.md). We allow 20 single URLs (AGENT_MAX_URLS) re-synced daily. A team moving from an old help center on another domain has hundreds of pages. First scope: add a site or sitemap URL, discover pages up to a cap (e.g. 500) with include/exclude path patterns, fetch through safeFetch with a crawl budget per cron tick, show the page list with status, and re-sync weekly.

title: Agents: Add WhatsApp as a channel for the agent
description: Chatbase deploys agents to WhatsApp (with templates and Coexistence), Messenger, Instagram and Slack (https://www.chatbase.co/docs/llms.txt) and Fin answers on WhatsApp, SMS and Slack (https://fin.ai/updates). Agents only run on a Chat widget, /a/<handle>, the API and Flow (AGENT_USAGE_CHANNELS). For small teams in LatAm WhatsApp is where customers write. First scope: connect a WhatsApp Business Cloud number to an agent, map each phone number to an agent conversation, run runAgent on inbound messages, reply within the 24 h window, and hand off to the Chat inbox (shared with the Chat WhatsApp channel idea) with the same handoff rules.

title: Agents: Run multi-turn simulations with an AI customer and replay real conversations
description: Fin Simulations play a full conversation with an AI customer, mock connector outputs and judge the result; Batch Test replays real conversations (https://fin.ai/updates/simulations-for-procedures, https://fin.ai/updates). Voiceflow tests support AI-simulated users with success criteria and assertions on tool calls (https://www.voiceflow.com/docs/documentation/measure/tests.md). Our tests (lib/agents-tests.ts) are one question plus an expected behavior, which does not cover booking or qualification flows. First scope: a test can be a persona plus a goal; an LLM plays the customer for up to N turns in dry run and the judge checks the goal and which tools were called; plus 'Replay last 20 conversations' that reruns real visitor messages against the current instructions and highlights answers that changed.

title: Agents: Score every conversation for sentiment and quality with AI
description: Fin rates every conversation with a CX Score without surveys and detects sentiment and urgency (https://community.intercom.com/product-updates/a-new-era-of-insights-has-arrived-10513); Chatbase shows sentiment and CSAT (https://www.chatbase.co/docs/user-guides/chatbot/analytics.md). Our Analytics tab (lib/agents-analytics.ts) has resolution, handoffs, tool errors, keyword topics and thumbs, which few visitors click. First scope: when a conversation goes idle, a cheap model call scores sentiment, whether the question was answered and a 1 to 5 quality score with a one-line reason; show averages and a worst-conversations list in Analytics and feed the existing alerts.

title: Agents: Show buttons and short forms in the chat to capture leads
description: Chatbase has Collect leads, Collect data, custom buttons and suggested messages as actions (https://www.chatbase.co/docs/llms.txt). Our agents ask for email and company in free text and then call crm_upsert_contact; visitors skip or mistype it and the SDR template loses leads. First scope: a collect_info tool the agent can call with fields (email, name, phone, company, a select) that renders a small form in the Chat widget and the public page, validates on the client, returns the values to the agent and saves them to the CRM contact, plus quick-reply buttons the agent can offer.

title: Agents: Connect MCP servers as tools
description: Fin added MCP connectors including a Zapier MCP that reaches thousands of apps (https://fin.ai/updates) and Voiceflow has an MCP tool (https://www.voiceflow.com/docs/documentation/build/tools/overview.md). Our tools are the suite tools plus http_request with secret headers (lib/agent-tools.ts), so calling a third-party system means hand-writing HTTP calls. First scope: add an MCP server URL with an optional secret header (reuse agent secrets), list its tools, enable specific tools per agent, run them through the existing logging, dry-run simulation and approval flow, and block private hosts with safeFetch.

title: Agents: Add step-by-step procedures the agent follows for a specific task
description: Fin Procedures combine natural-language steps with deterministic if/else, code and approval steps (https://fin.ai/help/en/articles/13976187-fin-procedures-explained); Chatbase has Procedures (https://chatbase.co/docs/user-guides/chatbot/procedures/procedures-overview.md) and Voiceflow mixes playbooks with canvas workflows. Our agent has one instruction block, so a refund or reschedule flow depends on the model following prose. First scope: named procedures with a trigger description and ordered steps (ask for a field, call a tool, check a condition, hand off); the runtime injects the active procedure and tracks the current step per conversation, and Analytics shows completion per procedure.

title: Agents: Export, import and duplicate an agent with its configuration
description: Chatbase lets you duplicate agents and Voiceflow exports environments (https://www.chatbase.co/docs/user-guides/chatbot/settings.md, https://www.voiceflow.com/docs/documentation/deploy/environments/overview.md). There is no way to copy an agent here: to try new instructions safely you rebuild it by hand, and there is no backup before a big edit. First scope: Duplicate in the agent menu, and export/import as JSON with instructions, knowledge selection, tools config, handoff, guardrails and tests (secrets excluded and listed as missing on import).

title: Agents: Fall back gracefully on the public page and API when the model fails
description: On the Chat channel a model failure falls back to the keyword bot (lib/agents-chat.ts), but on /a/<handle> the visitor sees the owner-facing error asking to load credits in the Vercel AI Gateway or choose a model in Instructions > Model (reproduced in the benchmark with ai_no_credits). Fin and Chatbase never show configuration errors to customers. First scope: map provider errors to a generic visitor message on the public page and API, offer handoff with an email field, record the error so the existing alerts notify the owner, and optionally retry with a fallback model.

title: Board: Generate a diagram from a text prompt with AI
description:
Excalidraw+ has chat-based text to diagram that streams onto the canvas (https://plus.excalidraw.com/changelog) and Miro's Create with AI builds diagrams and mind maps from a prompt (https://help.miro.com/hc/articles/28782102127890). Board only offers Mermaid to Excalidraw, which needs the user to write Mermaid. The AI gateway already powers Agents and Flow. First scope: a 'Generate' item next to Mermaid that sends the prompt to the AI gateway, asks for Mermaid flowchart, sequence or ER syntax, and inserts the converted elements at the viewport center as one undoable change.

Priority: high. Effort: M. Compared with Excalidraw+ / Miro.

title: Board: Open .excalidraw files and drop them on the canvas
description:
Excalidraw and Excalidraw+ open .excalidraw files and PNGs with an embedded scene (https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw). Board can save a .excalidraw file but cannot open one: the canvas menu sets loadScene: false (components/board/ExcalidrawCanvas.tsx) and the list has no import. A team switching from Excalidraw has its diagrams in those files. First scope: 'Import .excalidraw' on the board list that creates one board per file (images moved to Blob storage), plus dropping a file on an open board to merge its elements.

Priority: high. Effort: S. Compared with Excalidraw+.

title: Board: Group and summarize stickies with AI into a Docs page
description:
Miro AI clusters stickies by keyword or sentiment, summarizes them and turns them into a doc (https://help.miro.com/hc/articles/28781881506834). After a Board brainstorm or retro, sorting 60 stickies is manual. Board already knows stickies, their tags and their text (lib/board-stickies.ts) and Docs can create pages. First scope: with stickies selected, 'Group with AI' moves them into labeled columns inside a new frame, and 'Summarize to Docs' creates a page with the themes, vote counts and action items linked back to the board.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Miro.

title: Board: Add folders and search inside board content
description:
Excalidraw+ has unlimited folders and private collections, and full-text search across scenes is in progress (https://plus.excalidraw.com/pricing, https://plus.excalidraw.com/roadmap); Miro has spaces and search. The Board list and sidebar are flat and Cmd+K matches board names only. First scope: folders with the Link folders model shown in the list and sidebar, and Cmd+K results that match the text of stickies, shapes and frame names (indexed on save).

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Excalidraw+ / Miro.

title: Board: Expose boards through the public v1 API and MCP
description:
Excalidraw+ launched a public REST API for scenes, collections and logs (May 2026) and an MCP server with create_diagram and search_scene_content tools (https://plus.excalidraw.com/llms-full.txt); Miro has a REST API and MCP (https://miro.com/pricing/). app/api/v1 has no boards. First scope: GET and POST /api/v1/boards, GET /api/v1/boards/{id} with the scene, and POST /api/v1/boards/{id}/elements that accepts Excalidraw skeletons or Mermaid, behind boards:read and boards:write scopes, then the same as MCP tools.

Priority: medium. Effort: M. Compared with Excalidraw+ / Miro.

title: Board: Show a 'board changed' notice and refresh remote edits while the editor is open
description:
In Excalidraw+ every change appears for the other people at once (https://plus.excalidraw.com/pricing).
